title: Risk caps, lockouts & kill-switch
body:
## Context
E39 is the **safety scaffolding of the R3 "Trading on demo" train**. The roadmap is explicit that it lands *before* any order-placing UI ships: `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.3 rule 2 — "No order-placing UI ships before the key vault (E27), risk caps and kill-switch (E39), and the native-SL invariant (E32) are Done — this ordering is a safety requirement, not a preference." The dependency graph in `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 encodes it: `E27 --> E39`, `E39 --> E32`, `E39 --> E42`, `E39 --> E44`.

The epic delivers backend module **M17** behaviour (the risk/limit enforcement layer described in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10 `Validator` and `KillSwitch` rows) plus the owner-facing surfaces that make it operable: the risk dashboard, the lockout notice, the kill-switch confirmation modal and the global risk policy admin page.

Three product principles drive the whole design:
1. **Server-side authority** (`20-architecture.md` §1 principle P8): "The frontend is never trusted for account scope, risk caps or environment." Every cap, every lockout and the kill-switch are evaluated inside the order path in the backend, never in the client.
2. **Stops new risk, does not force-close** — the kill-switch semantics locked in `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E39 row. Flattening is a *separate, explicitly-opted-in* action (`POST /api/v1/positions/close-all`) with its own documented runbook.
3. **Every transition is audited, and step-up gated wherever it loosens safety** — `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-025 requires step-up re-authentication for "changing risk caps or per-account profiles, disabling the kill switch"; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §12 lists clearing a risk lockout among step-up actions.

Plan references: `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §19 POS and §26 ADMIN, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-071/072/073/134, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/risk/summary`, `/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override`, `/trading/kill-switch`, `/me/limits`), `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 `SystemUpdate`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.3/§3.3/§3.9.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (Must/Should from the epic's domains POS + ADMIN and their risk siblings):**
- **US-PROF-004** Risk caps enforced server-side (Must) — the order-path enforcement engine.
- **US-RULE-012** Daily loss limit and lockout (Must) — automatic lockout, flatten-per-policy hook, day-boundary reset, step-up override.
- **US-RULE-014** Owner kill-switch (Must) — per-manager FREEZE and global kill-switch, ≤2 s server-side effectiveness.
- **US-ADMIN-003** Risk-limit administration (Must) — per-manager limits, tighten-during-open-position semantics, audit of every change.
- **US-ADMIN-004** Owner risk dashboard (Must) — SCR-071 aggregate risk view with per-account cap utilisation and FREEZE controls.
- **US-POS-009** Closed positions and daily PnL (Must) — **only** the day-boundary definition and the realised-PnL feed the daily-loss cap consumes; the grid itself is E29.
- **US-POS-006** Account and group filtering (Must) — **only** the server-side manager scoping of `/risk/summary`; the grid filtering UI is E29.

Out-of-epic consumers: E30 order ticket shows remaining headroom from `/me/limits`; E34 fan-out pre-validates caps per leg; E35 rule runtime honours `sys.daily_loss_lockout`; E42 admin screens embed the kill-switch in the flag console.

**Screens:** SCR-071 Risk dashboard · SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation modal · SCR-073 Lockout notice (manager view) · SCR-134 Admin: risk policy (global).
**Components:** CMP-117 RiskLockoutBanner · CMP-138 RiskCapMeter · CMP-211 PanicButtons · CMP-123 FlattenAllButton · CMP-044 ConfirmDialog · CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger · CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError · CMP-028 Callout/Banner · CMP-035 Countdown/Timer · CMP-049 Table · CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect · CMP-116 PnLBadge · CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart · CMP-178 SystemHealthTile · CMP-008 NumericStepperInput · CMP-040 FormField · CMP-065 FormSection · CMP-087 AdminLayout.
**API:** `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` · `POST /api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override` · `GET|POST /api/v1/trading/kill-switch` · `GET /api/v1/me/limits` · `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all` (referenced, owned by E29) · admin risk-policy CRUD.
**WS:** topic `system` (`SystemUpdate` with `kind: "kill_switch"` and `kind: "notice"` for lockouts, `severity: critical`), and the `risk_cap_usage` field on the account-status payload (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15).
**DB tables:** `account_profiles` (cap columns `max_position_notional_usd`, `max_daily_loss_usd`, `max_open_positions`, `max_orders_per_minute`), `user_account_access` (`frozen`, `frozen_at`, `frozen_by`, `frozen_reason`, `max_daily_loss_usd`), `positions`, `position_snapshots` (`reason='risk_eval'`), `feature_flags` (`is_killswitch`), `audit_log`, `system_events`, plus the new `risk_lockouts`, `risk_policy` and `kill_switch_state` tables introduced by E39-T02.

## Out of scope
- Flatten-all execution mechanics and `POST /positions/close-all` implementation (E29 OMS core) — E39 only *calls* it and documents the runbook.
- The native exchange-side SL invariant itself (E32/M17 `NativeStopGuard`); E39 surfaces `positions_without_native_stop` from `RiskSummary` but does not enforce it.
- The rate-limit token-bucket governor for fan-out (E34); E39 owns only the user-facing `max_orders_per_minute` **risk cap**, not exchange rate budgeting.
- Rule-engine authored risk rules and the dead-man's switch (US-RULE-013 → E35).
- Per-account profile CRUD screens and the profile schema (E28); E39 consumes `RiskCaps`.
- Live-environment gating (E44) and the audit hash-chain browser (E42).
- Android, a separate admin app, and any non-Bybit-USDT-perp instrument.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A cap breach is refused inside the order path
  Given account C has max_position_notional_usd 25000 and holds 20000 of notional
  When any client (ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule action, fan-out leg, emulated algo child) submits an order adding 10000 of notional
  Then the order is rejected with RFC 9457 code "risk_limit_breached" before any exchange call
  And the rejection names the cap, the limit and the current value
  And an audit row is written

Scenario: Daily loss breach locks the account out
  Given account C has max_daily_loss_usd 1500 and realised+unrealised PnL reaches -1500
  When the risk evaluator next runs (within 5 s, and immediately on the triggering execution event)
  Then the account enters lockout, working orders are cancelled per policy, new entries are refused and reduce-only remains allowed
  And every session holding that account receives a "system" WS frame within 500 ms and shows SCR-073
  And the lockout ends at the configured day boundary unless overridden

Scenario: Kill-switch stops new risk everywhere without closing positions
  Given open positions and armed rules exist across 5 accounts
  When the owner engages the global kill-switch
  Then within 2 s every order-placement path is refused server-side with "trading_disabled"
  And every armed rule is disarmed
  And open positions are untouched unless flatten_positions was explicitly checked
  And one audit record per affected entity is written

Scenario (failure): Risk evaluator is unavailable
  Given the risk evaluator cannot compute caps for an account
  When an order is submitted for it
  Then the order is refused fail-closed with "risk_state_unavailable", never admitted optimistically
  And the risk dashboard marks the account "stale"

Scenario (edge): Tightening a limit below current exposure
  Given a manager holds exposure exceeding a newly tightened limit
  When the owner saves the tighter limit
  Then no forced liquidation occurs, new entries are blocked, reduce-only actions remain available
  And both owner and manager are informed and the change is audited with old and new values
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Module M17** lives at `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/` with a pure evaluator (`evaluate(account_state, caps, command) -> Decision`) so it is unit-testable without I/O, plus a stateful `RiskService` maintaining per-account rolling counters (daily realised PnL, unrealised PnL, open positions, orders-in-last-60s) fed from the OMS event bus (`oms.*`) and `position_snapshots`.
- The evaluator is invoked from the OMS `Validator` (`20-architecture.md` §3.10) *before* sizing and before any exchange call; budget ≤5 ms p95 (US-PROF-004 and US-ADMIN-003 NFRs).
- Kill-switch state is one row per scope, read through a cache with 5 s max staleness; `feature_flags.is_killswitch` rows bypass caching per `21-database-schema.md` §3.9. Reads are fail-closed: if state cannot be read, trading is refused.
- Error codes: `risk_limit_breached` (422, already in the `22-api-openapi.yaml` problem catalogue), `trading_disabled` (kill-switch refusal), `account_locked` (also a fan-out leg rejection code), `risk_state_unavailable` (new, 503).
- Audit actions: `risk.freeze`, `risk.unfreeze`, `risk.lockout_triggered`, `risk.lockout_overridden` (high severity), `risk.auto_flatten`, `risk_cap.changed`, `risk_policy.updated`.
- Step-up (`POST /auth/step-up`, `elevated_until = now + 15 min`) is mandatory for: releasing the kill-switch, overriding a lockout, editing any cap or the global risk policy (SR-025).

## Test plan
Rolled up from children: unit (evaluator decision table, day-boundary arithmetic, fail-closed paths), contract (OpenAPI + `SystemUpdate` schema), integration (recorded Bybit fixtures with partial fills driving PnL across the cap), E2E (Playwright web + Electron for SCR-071/072/073/134), perf (cap evaluation ≤5 ms p95, kill-switch propagation ≤2 s and server refusal ≤200 ms), chaos (backend restart mid-lockout, Postgres failover during freeze, WS disconnect during breach), a11y (axe + screen-reader passes), security (abuse cases per E39-X02). Coverage floor ≥90 % on M17 by local policy (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 Coverage row).

## Security notes
STRIDE areas touched: elevation of privilege (a manager engaging a global freeze, self-overriding a lockout), tampering (client-side cap bypass; the feature-flag route used to disable the kill-switch — threat D2 in `04-security-program.md` §5), repudiation (an unaudited freeze), denial of service (freeze used maliciously to strand positions). Controls: SR-025 step-up, SR-055 owner-only scope rules, SR-067 role-scoped audit reads, server-side-only evaluation (P8). Data classification: financial state plus account identifiers; no secrets. The epic carries the `security` label; Critical/High STRIDE findings must be closed before the R3 gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA across SCR-071/072/073/134. Non-negotiables from the catalogue: every state text-labelled (`ok`/`WARN`/`LOCK`, never colour alone); meters expose numeric values; the kill-switch modal is `role="alertdialog"` with focus starting on Cancel and a single blast-radius confirm whose button names the effect (no typed word, no hold, no step-up to engage); the lockout notice is `role="alert"` on appearance and persists as a banner; panic controls are never icon-only and the hold-to-confirm gesture has a keyboard equivalent.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: cap evaluation adds ≤5 ms p95 to the order path (inside budget #4 "order submit → ack p95 < 300 ms" on demo, a hard R3 gate); the kill-switch halts acceptance server-side within 200 ms of the backend call (SCR-072); the lockout notice is visible client-side within 500 ms of the breach (SCR-073); risk-dashboard aggregates are recomputed server-side, UI updates at ≤1 Hz and never block trading surfaces (SCR-071).

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_risk_eval_duration_seconds` (histogram), `cv_risk_cap_utilisation_ratio{account,cap}`, `cv_risk_lockouts_active`, `cv_kill_switch_engaged` (gauge 0/1), `cv_risk_rejections_total{code}`, `cv_risk_state_stale_accounts`. Structured logs on every decision with `request_id` correlation. Traces spanning Validator→RiskService. Audit events as listed above. Grafana panel "Risk & safety" with alerts on `cv_kill_switch_engaged == 1` and `cv_risk_state_stale_accounts > 0`.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2: every child Done; epic-level AC verified end-to-end on demo; coverage ≥90 % on M17 and ≥80 % frontend; docs (`20-architecture.md`, `21-database-schema.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`) reflect shipped behaviour; ADR-0016 merged; a11y pass on all four screens; perf numbers recorded; STRIDE finalised with Critical/High closed and Security sign-off; epic-level QA regression pass; demoed to Owner at Sprint Review; retro notes filed.

## Dependencies
- `E27` Accounts, sub-accounts & API-key vault — accounts, `user_account_access`, and the step-up/2FA plumbing the lockout override requires (roadmap edge `E27 --> E39`).
- `E29` OMS core & order state machine — the `Validator` hook point, the order/position event stream, and `POST /positions/close-all`.
- `E28` Per-account profiles & trade groups — the `RiskCaps` schema on `account_profiles` that E39 enforces.
- `E09` Auth, sessions, 2FA & RBAC — step-up re-authentication and role scoping.
Downstream: `E32`, `E42`, `E44` are blocked by this epic.

## Branch
`feat/e39-risk-caps` (umbrella naming; children use `feat/e39-<short>`). PR size guidance: ≤400 LOC diff per PR; the evaluator, the enforcement hook and each screen ship as separate PRs.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. title: UX research and wireframes for risk caps, lockout and kill-switch flows
body:
## Context
E39 introduces four screens the product has never had: an aggregate **risk dashboard** (SCR-071), a **kill-switch/freeze confirmation** (SCR-072), a **lockout notice** the user cannot dismiss (SCR-073), and a **global risk policy** admin page (SCR-134). Three of them are *interruption* surfaces — they appear when something has gone wrong and the user is under stress — which makes them new interaction territory and triggers the `ux-research` requirement in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence.

The design-ahead rule applies: the consuming FE stories E39-S04 and E39-S05 are scheduled for Sprint 16, so this research + wireframe ticket must be Done by end of Sprint 13, and the hi-fi tickets (E39-D02, E39-D03) by end of Sprint 14.

Key behavioural constraint to design against, from `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2: the kill-switch **"stops new risk, does not force-close"**. Every screen must make that distinction unmissable, because the single most dangerous misunderstanding in this epic is a user believing FREEZE closed their positions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Owner + Manager walkthroughs (2 scripted sessions) covering: what the owner expects FREEZE to do; what a manager needs to know the moment a lockout hits; which figure they look at first on a risk dashboard.
- Low-fi wireframes for **SCR-071**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-073**, **SCR-134**, matching the ASCII layouts already in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` and either confirming or explicitly superseding them (a supersession requires a note here plus a PR to the catalogue).
- State inventories per screen, per catalogue convention: SCR-071 normal · warning (≥80 % of a cap) · locked · frozen · stale data · reconciling; SCR-072 executing (per-account progress) · completed summary · partial failure with retry; SCR-073 active lockout · override-requested · expired; SCR-134 clean · validation warning (portfolio cap below the sum of per-account caps) · step-up required · save conflict.
- Copy deck for the danger wording: the FREEZE consequence restatement ("This cancels 14 working orders and blocks new orders on 5 accounts. Open positions are NOT closed."), lockout reason strings for each `RiskSummary.accounts[].lockout.reason` enum value (`daily_loss`, `consecutive_losses`, `max_positions`, `manual`), and the override reason-field helper text.
- Flow diagram updating `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F20 with the breach → lockout → override path.
- Research findings written into the ticket and linked from the `14-screens-catalogue.md` sign-off checklists.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi visual design, tokens and motion (E39-D02, E39-D03).
- The order ticket's inline cap-headroom chip (CMP-232 LimitsChip) — owned by E30.
- Any Figma prototype of the trade-group fan-out preview (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Research questions answered
  Given two owner/manager sessions are completed
  When the findings are written up
  Then each of the three research questions has a recorded answer with supporting quotes
  And at least one wireframe decision is explicitly attributed to a finding

Scenario: Every state is drawn
  Given the wireframe set is submitted for review
  Then every state listed in this ticket's Scope exists as a distinct frame
  And no frame relies on colour alone to convey ok / WARN / LOCK

Scenario (failure case): Ambiguous freeze copy is rejected
  Given a reviewer reads the SCR-072 copy deck without prior context
  When asked "does this close my positions?"
  Then they answer "no" correctly, otherwise the copy is reworked before sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes are produced in Figma in the `CandleViewer / R3 Trading` file, page `E39 Risk & safety`. Frames are named `SCR-0nn / <state>` so the handoff ticket can link them one-to-one with catalogue entries. The data shapes to design against are real: `RiskSummary` (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) for SCR-071, `KillSwitchResult.actions` for SCR-072's completion summary, and the `RiskCaps` field set for SCR-134.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Validation is the moderated walkthrough: both participants complete "freeze sub_001 without closing its positions" and "explain why trading is blocked" on the wireframes without facilitator help.

## Security notes
Research sessions must not capture real API keys, balances or screenshots of live credentials; use the fixture account labels (`Main`, `sub_001`, `sub_002`) from the catalogue. Data classification: internal only.

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes must already encode the a11y contracts from the catalogue: text labels for every status, numeric values beside every meter, `role="alertdialog"` structure for SCR-072 with focus starting on Cancel, `role="alert"` for SCR-073, and a radio-group enforcement-scope selector on SCR-134. The a11y specialist reviews at wireframe stage, not only at hi-fi.

## Performance notes
Designs must not require data the backend cannot deliver at the ≤1 Hz aggregate refresh (SCR-071 performance note); no per-tick animated figure on the dashboard.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Two research sessions run and written up.
- [ ] Wireframe set covers all four screens and every enumerated state.
- [ ] Copy deck reviewed by the Owner.
- [ ] `13-user-flows.md` F20 updated by PR.
- [ ] a11y specialist review comment present.
- [ ] CDO/design-lead sign-off recorded (Status Done) — this is the gate for E39-D02/E39-D03.

## Dependencies
No blockers. Consumed by E39-D02 and E39-D03.

## Branch
`design/e39-risk-wireframes`. Docs-only PR (flows + catalogue notes), ≤200 LOC.

## References

- `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F20
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E39 row
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`

## Context
Hi-fi design for the two *action* surfaces of E39: **SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation modal** and **SCR-134 Admin: risk policy (global)** (route `/admin/risk-policy`), plus the **CMP-211 PanicButtons** cluster that lives permanently in the app-shell top bar (SCR-010). These are the highest-consequence controls in the product: a mis-designed confirmation here is a trading incident, which is why this design ticket is P0.

`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-072 fixes the hard requirements: the modal names exactly which accounts and users are affected, restates the consequence in text ("This cancels 14 working orders and blocks new orders on 5 accounts. Open positions are NOT closed."), is confirmed by one blast-radius Confirm whose button names the effect (no typed word, no hold, no step-up — architect ruling on #829, 2026-10-14), and offers "also cancel working orders" (default **on**, the API default) and "also flatten positions" (default **off**) as explicit checkboxes.

Consumed by E39-S05 in Sprint 16 → Done required by end of Sprint 14 (design-ahead rule).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-072**: scope selector (this account / all accounts; per-symbol scope is not in the API — OD-7 in `docs/design/E39/E39-D01.md`; a mixed-environment account set is refused and global covers every environment, D-3) · consequence restatement with live counts · the single blast-radius confirm (button label names the effect; flatten opt-in changes the label; `reason` pre-filled) · the two opt-in checkboxes · executing (per-account progress) · completed summary driven by `KillSwitchResult.actions` (`orders_cancelled`, `positions_flattened`, `rules_disarmed`) · partial failure with per-account retry · the **unfreeze** path with its own confirmation and step-up · DEMO vs LIVE variants (global covers every environment; the per-account blast-radius rows carry their environment, D-3) · the manager variant per D-1 (within grants, never flatten, owner paged) · engaged-but-not-durable (`persisted: false`, SR-E39-05) and automatic (`KILL`, `engaged_by: system`) variants.
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-134**: every global limit drawn with units (max daily loss, max drawdown, max total notional, max positions, max leverage, max orders/min, per-symbol concentration) · breach-behaviour selector per limit (warn / block new orders / flatten) · the current measured value beside each limit · per-user and per-account override visibility · the "this cannot be disabled entirely" guard · step-up gate on save · change summary before save · the validation warning when a portfolio cap is below the sum of the smallest per-account caps.
- **CMP-211 PanicButtons** spec: the Flatten-all / Cancel-all / Kill-switch cluster for `scope: account|group|global`, `confirmMode: hold|typed|single`, enabled/disabled (Viewer) states, and the hold-confirmation progress treatment with its keyboard equivalent. PR to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`.
- **Global hotkey treatment**: the roadmap requires the kill-switch to be flippable "from the admin screen and from a global hotkey" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2). Design the hotkey's on-screen affordance, its discoverability in the hotkey cheatsheet (SCR-013), and the confirmation it still requires — the hotkey opens SCR-072, it never fires directly.
- Formal **a11y review** of both screens and the **handoff package** for E39-S05 (redlines, token map, field→element mapping against `SetKillSwitchRequest` / `KillSwitchResult`).

## Out of scope
- SCR-071 / SCR-073 (E39-D02).
- The flatten-all *runbook* text (E39-T03).
- The feature-flag console that also exposes the kill-switch (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Consequence is unambiguous
  Given a reviewer with no prior context reads the SCR-072 primary frame
  When asked whether open positions will be closed
  Then they answer "no" for the default frame and "yes" for the flatten-ticked frame without the facilitator explaining

Scenario: Defaults are safe
  Given the SCR-072 frame as first rendered
  Then "also cancel working orders" is checked and "also flatten positions" is unchecked (API defaults)
  And the primary action is not the default-focused control
  And ticking "also flatten positions" checks and disables "also cancel working orders" with a reason (flatten implies cancel)

Scenario: Partial failure is a first-class frame
  Given a freeze where 1 of 5 accounts failed
  Then a frame shows which account failed, why, and a per-account retry
  And the succeeded accounts are not re-executed by that retry
  And no frame calls the freeze complete before the exchange verification read (SR-E39-06)

Scenario: Manager engagement per D-1
  Given a manager opens SCR-072 for a granted account
  Then "also flatten positions" is disabled with the reason "Only the owner can flatten" and "All accounts" is disabled with the reason "Global freeze is owner-only"
  And the consequence text says the owner is notified and that only the owner can release

Scenario: Policy floors and the override allowance
  Given the SCR-134 frames
  Then the degraded-trading block is a fixed-on rule, lockout minutes are bounded 1..1440, a removed limit is refused (D-5) and a "save refused — policy floor" frame exists
  And the override policy fieldset shows `override_extra_loss_max_usd` (default 0) and the owner-override frame carries the `extra_loss_usd` allowance (D-4)

Scenario (edge): SCR-134 conflicting caps
  Given a portfolio cap lower than the sum of the smallest per-account caps
  Then an explanatory warning frame exists naming which caps conflict
```

## Technical notes / design
Figma page `E39 Risk & safety`, frames `SCR-072 / <state>`, `SCR-134 / <state>`, `CMP-211 / <variant>`. SCR-072 composes CMP-044 ConfirmDialog (`variant="standard"`; CMP-211 `confirmMode: "single"` for the kill switch), CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton and CMP-027 ErrorState. SCR-134 composes CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 and CMP-138. The completion summary must render zero counts gracefully ("0 orders cancelled — none were working").

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification is the moderated comprehension test in the acceptance criteria plus the exported-token contrast check.

## Security notes
Step-up authentication (SR-025) is a **drawn step**, not an implied one, for: releasing the kill-switch, saving SCR-134, and any override. The modal must never render an account's API key, fingerprint or balance detail beyond what SCR-071 already shows. SCR-072 is `role="alertdialog"`; the exact consequence is restated in text; confirmation is a single activation of the named Confirm reached by Tab, Enter; **focus starts on the Cancel control**; the hold-to-confirm gesture on CMP-211 exposes progress via `aria-valuenow` and has a keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`); panic buttons are never icon-only and carry scope in their accessible name ("Flatten all positions — all accounts"). title: Spike: authoritative daily-PnL source and day-boundary semantics for the loss cap

## Context
The daily-loss cap is the cap most likely to be wrong, because "daily loss" is not one number. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-RULE-012 NFR says it is "computed server-side from realised plus unrealised PnL; evaluated on every position/execution event and at least every 5 s". US-POS-009 says "'today' uses the configured day boundary consistently with the daily-loss limit" and warns that fee data may arrive late ("the row shows the PnL as provisional and updates when fees settle"). `24-internal-schemas.md` §11 `sys.daily_loss_lockout` states the built-in rule halts new orders "until next UTC day".

Three sources can supply the number and they disagree: (a) locally-aggregated `executions` + `positions` state, (b) Bybit `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl`, (c) wallet equity deltas. They differ by fee settlement timing, funding attribution, and the exchange's own day boundary. ## Scope / Deliverables

- A decision on the evaluation cadence that satisfies "every position/execution event and at least every 5 s" without exceeding the reconciliation rate budget (US-POS-008 NFR: "reconciliation must not exceed the rate budget").
- **ADR-0016** draft section covering the chosen source and boundary (the full ADR is authored in E39-T03).
- Follow-up tickets filed for whatever the chosen path needs that is not already in E39-T01.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the evaluator (E39-T01).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
  And each divergence episode is attributed to a named cause

Scenario: Decision recorded with criteria met
  Given the decision criteria stated up front (accuracy within 0.5% of exchange truth, availability without an extra REST call on the hot path, determinism under replay)
  When one source satisfies all three
  Then it is chosen and recorded; if none does, a hybrid is specified explicitly rather than left to implementation

Scenario (failure): Fee-lag worst case
  Given a close whose fees settle 90 seconds later
  Then the spike states what the evaluator does in that window: lock provisionally, defer, or lock on the pessimistic bound
  And the chosen behaviour is justified against "a bad day cannot become a disaster"
```

## Technical notes / design
Decision criteria, agreed before starting:
1. Accuracy within 0.5 % of `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` over the window.
2. Obtainable without an additional REST call on the order hot path (the evaluator has a ≤5 ms p95 budget, so it must read cached/streamed state).
3. Deterministic under replay (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3 exit criterion 6 requires rule-runtime determinism over replay; the risk evaluator shares that constraint because lockouts feed rule behaviour).
If the local aggregation is within 0.5 % it wins on criteria 2 and 3; otherwise a hybrid (local for the hot path, periodic REST reconciliation that can *tighten* but never silently *loosen* an active lockout) is specified.

Harness-level only: a comparison script under `tools/spikes/e39-daily-pnl/` with recorded fixtures checked in so the numbers are reproducible. No coverage target (throwaway code, stated explicitly per DoR §5.1).

The harness uses demo keys only, read through the E27 key vault interface — never plaintext keys in the spike code or in checked-in fixtures. Fixtures must be scrubbed of account identifiers before commit. A wrong decision here is a *safety* finding, so the Security engineer reviews the conclusion even though the spike ships no code.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
The chosen source must be readable within the ≤5 ms p95 evaluator budget; the spike records the measured read latency of each candidate.

The spike specifies which metric exposes the divergence in production: `cv_risk_pnl_divergence_usd{account,source}`, alerting above a threshold set by the measured worst case.

title: Black-box test plan, risk fixtures and regression pack for caps and lockouts
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` requires "black-box QA test plans + white-box review per feature", and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded QA sign-off a hard gate on every Story. E39's risk caps and lockouts cannot be exercised by waiting for real losses, so the first deliverable here is a **deterministic fixture harness** that can drive any account to any cap state on demand; everything else in E39's QA (E39-Q02 E2E, E39-Q03 perf/chaos, E39-D04 design QA) depends on it.

R3 quality gate: "the native-SL invariant suite, kill-switch suite and risk-cap suite are **required checks**; a failure blocks merge, not just release" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 Safety row). This ticket builds the risk-cap half of that required check.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Fixture harness** `tests/fixtures/risk/` with a seeding API (`seed_risk_state(account, *, realised_pnl, unrealised_pnl, open_positions, notional, orders_last_minute, consecutive_losses)`) that drives the M17 counters deterministically, plus recorded Bybit demo fixtures for: a sequence of partial fills walking PnL to exactly the daily cap; a sequence overshooting it in one fill; a position-count sequence reaching the concurrent cap; and a late-fee-settlement case (the US-POS-009 "provisional PnL" edge).
- **Black-box test plan** (`docs/qa/e39-risk-caps-plan.md`) covering E39-S01 and E39-S02 as a user would exercise them: one scenario per cap × {under, at, over}, the reduce-only exemption, manager scoping of `/risk/summary`, viewer 403 on partial aggregates, lockout trigger/expiry/override, and the stale-state refusal. Each scenario states preconditions, steps, expected result and the evidence to capture.
- **Regression pack**: the plan's scenarios encoded as an automated suite (`tests/regression/risk/`) registered as a **required check** in CI per the R3 safety gate, runnable against demo in under 10 minutes.
- **Boundary-value matrix**: for every numeric cap, tests at limit−ε, limit, limit+ε, zero, null/unset, and the schema maximum (`max_orders_per_minute` 600, `max_open_positions` 100, `lockout_minutes_after_breach` 1440) — the API and DB bounds must agree.
- QA sign-off record template for E39-S01/S02 with pass/fail per scenario.

## Out of scope
- Kill-switch E2E (E39-Q02) and perf/chaos (E39-Q03).
- a11y auditing (E39-Q04).
- Unit tests owned by the implementing tickets — this is black-box, exercising the running system through its API.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Any cap state is reachable on demand
  Given the fixture harness
  When a tester requests an account at 99% of its daily-loss cap
  Then the system reports that state within one evaluation cycle
  And the state is reproducible across runs

Scenario: Plan covers every cap
  Given the black-box plan
  Then every cap enumerated in RiskCaps and account_profiles has at least three scenarios (under, at, over)
  And the reduce-only exemption has its own scenario per cap

Scenario: Regression pack gates merges
  Given a change that removes the concurrent-positions check
  When CI runs
  Then the risk-cap required check fails and the merge is blocked

Scenario (edge): Provisional fees
  Given a close whose fees settle after the evaluation
  Then a scenario asserts the documented behaviour from E39-K01 (provisional vs settled locking) rather than leaving it undefined
```

## Technical notes / design
The harness seeds through an internal test-only endpoint guarded by an environment check (`CV_ENV in {dev, test}`) plus a build flag, so it cannot exist in a staging or live build — a test asserts the endpoint returns 404 when the flag is off. Recorded fixtures are stored as replayable exchange responses in `packages/fixtures/bybit/` (the `risk/` set), in a capture's dated directory, each file with its `manifest.json` entry (`packages/fixtures/bybit/README.md`), using the existing recorded-fixture format from `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Test plan
Meta: the harness itself has unit tests (seeding produces the requested counters; the guard blocks non-dev environments). The regression pack runs against the demo environment in CI nightly and on every PR touching `cvapi/oms/`.

## Security notes
The test-only seeding endpoint is a **privilege-escalation surface if it ever ships** — hence the double guard (env + build flag) and an explicit test asserting its absence in a production-profile build. Fixtures must contain no real account identifiers or key material. This ticket is reviewed by the Security engineer for that reason despite being a QA ticket.

N/A — API-level testing. (a11y is E39-Q04.)

## Performance notes
The regression pack must complete in ≤10 minutes so it can be a required check without throttling the merge queue; scenarios share seeded state where independence allows.

## Observability
Each regression run publishes pass/fail per scenario and the observed breach→lockout latency, feeding the same `cv_risk_breach_to_notice_seconds` budget tracked in production.

title: E2E suite proving no order path escapes the kill-switch or a lockout
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion 7 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3) states the bar exactly: "Kill-switch works end-to-end: activated, no new order can be placed **by any path including the rule engine**; existing positions untouched; released cleanly; every transition audited." Exit criterion 2 establishes the pattern this suite copies from the native-SL invariant: "an automated test suite attempts, by every available path (ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule action, fan-out, emulated algo), to open a position… all attempts are rejected, logged, and audited. **Zero escapes.**"

This ticket builds the kill-switch/lockout equivalent as a Playwright suite over web + Electron, and it is the acceptance evidence for E39-S03, E39-S04 and E39-S05.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright suite `e2e/risk/` running against **web and the Electron shell** (both are required by the R3 E2E gate), using the E39-Q01 fixture harness for deterministic state.
- **Zero-escape matrix**: with the kill-switch engaged, attempt to place an order from every available path and assert refusal, an audit row, and a user-visible reason for each: (1) order ticket SCR-060, (2) chart order-line drag SCR-030, (3) DOM ladder click, (4) rule-engine action, (5) trade-group fan-out leg, (6) emulated-algo child, (7) direct API call with a valid session (bypassing the UI entirely — the path a hostile client would use). Paths whose owning epic has not yet shipped (e.g. emulated algos, E33) are present as `test.fixme` placeholders with the owning epic named, so the matrix is visibly incomplete rather than silently missing rows.
- **Positions-untouched assertion**: after a default-options engagement, position count and sizes are byte-identical to before.
- **Lockout equivalent**: the same matrix with a daily-loss lockout instead of the kill-switch, additionally asserting that reduce-only closes **succeed** throughout.
- **Release flow**: owner unfreeze with step-up → order placement works again → rules remain disarmed until explicitly re-armed.
- **UI propagation**: SCR-073 appears in the order ticket, the positions grid and the risk dashboard within 500 ms of the breach frame; the kill-switch frame disables order-entry affordances without a REST round-trip (this is WS conformance case **C12** in `23-ws-protocol.md` §16 — "Disable order-entry affordances on `kill_switch.engaged`").
- **Audit completeness**: after each scenario, query the audit log and assert one row per affected entity with the expected action name and severity.
- Registration of the suite as part of the R3 **required checks** (safety gate).

## Out of scope
- Load and chaos testing (E39-Q03).
- a11y auditing (E39-Q04) — though the suite uses accessible selectors, which surfaces gross a11y breakage early.
- Unit/contract tests owned by the implementing stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Zero escapes with the kill-switch engaged
  Given the kill-switch is engaged globally
  When an order is attempted from every path in the matrix
  Then every attempt is refused with trading_disabled
  And every attempt produces an audit row
  And the user sees an explanatory reason on each surface

Scenario: Positions are untouched
  Given three open positions and default freeze options
  When the kill-switch is engaged
  Then the position count and sizes are unchanged afterwards

Scenario: Reduce-only survives a lockout
  Given an account in a daily-loss lockout
  When a reduce-only close is submitted from the positions grid
  Then it succeeds
  And an opening order from the same grid is refused

Scenario: WS-driven affordance disable (C12)
  Given the order ticket is open
  When a kill_switch frame arrives on the system topic
  Then the submit control becomes unavailable with an explanation
  And no REST round-trip was required to reach that state

Scenario (failure): A newly added order path is not gated
  Given a developer adds a seventh order path without gating it
  When the suite runs
  Then the matrix's path-registry assertion fails, naming the ungated path
```

## Technical notes / design
The path registry is shared with the backend's origin registry test (E39-S01) via a checked-in list `contracts/order-origins.json`, so backend and E2E cannot drift: adding an origin in one place without the other fails CI. Playwright projects: `web-chromium` and `electron`. Each scenario tears down by releasing the switch and clearing lockouts through the harness, so scenarios are order-independent and parallelisable.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan; its own meta-checks are: the suite fails when enforcement is deliberately disabled via a mutation test (a CI job that runs the suite against a build with `risk.enforcement` stubbed out and asserts the suite goes red — proving the suite has teeth rather than passing vacuously).

## Security notes
This suite is the practical proof of the product's core safety control, so its integrity matters as much as the feature's. The mutation check above prevents a vacuously-passing suite. The suite must not embed real credentials; it authenticates through the standard demo test-user flow. Findings from this suite that reveal a bypass are **security** incidents and route to E39-X02, not just to a Bug.

## Accessibility notes
Selectors use accessible roles and names (`getByRole('alertdialog')`, `getByRole('button', {name: /Flatten all positions/})`), which doubles as a smoke test that the a11y contracts from E39-D03 actually shipped.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock ≤15 minutes across both projects so it is viable as a required check. It asserts the 500 ms breach→notice and 2 s freeze-effectiveness budgets as test assertions, not just as monitored metrics.

## Observability
Each run publishes the zero-escape matrix as a table artefact (path × outcome) attached to the CI run, so a reviewer can see coverage at a glance rather than reading logs.

title: Performance and chaos scenarios for risk evaluation and kill-switch propagation
body:
## Context
Two E39 numbers are hard gates rather than aspirations. Cap evaluation must add **≤5 ms p95** to the order path (US-PROF-004 and US-ADMIN-003 NFRs) inside budget #4 — "Order submit → ack p95 < 300 ms (demo), **hard for demo (R3 exit gate)**" (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2). The kill-switch must be **effective within 2 s** (US-RULE-014 NFR) with a **200 ms** server-side halt (SCR-072). And the R3 chaos gate requires "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out — all resume to a correct, reconciled state" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4); E39's share is proving that risk state and kill-switch state survive those events **fail-closed**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **k6 load script** `perf/k6/e39-risk.js`: sustained order submission across 5 demo accounts at the per-UID limit for 1 hour (matching the R3 Load gate), measuring the risk-gate contribution via the `risk.evaluate` span and asserting p95 ≤5 ms and no drift over the hour (the counters are in-memory and must not degrade as the day's event history grows).
- **Kill-switch propagation benchmark**: under that load, engage the switch and measure (a) time to first server-side refusal, (b) time to the WS frame at a connected client, (c) time until every connected session's order affordances are disabled. Assert 200 ms / 2 s.
- **Chaos scenarios** (using the existing chaos harness from `03-testing-strategy.md`):
  1. **Backend restart while a lockout is active** — the lockout is still in force afterwards; accounts are not silently unlocked; the daily counter is rebuilt from `executions`, not reset to zero.
  2. **Backend restart while the kill-switch is engaged** — it comes back engaged; if the state read fails during startup, trading is refused (fail-closed), not permitted.
  3. **Postgres failover during kill-switch engagement** — the switch either completes or reports per-account failures; it never reports success for an account whose state was not written.
  4. **WS disconnect between breach and push** — the client, on reconnect, learns of the lockout from the snapshot rather than only from the missed delta (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11 restore order).
  5. **Exchange 5xx / rate-limit 10018 during lockout-driven cancellation** — cancellation retries with back-off, the lockout remains in force, and the failure is visible rather than swallowed.
  6. **Clock skew** — an evaluator clock skewed past the day boundary must not release a lockout early; the boundary is computed from a monotonic server time source with skew detection.
- Recorded results appended to the performance report and to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` if a new risk surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E (E39-Q02) and a11y (E39-Q04).
- Engine FPS / rendering budgets (chart-engine epics).
- Bybit-side rate-limit governor tuning (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Risk gate stays inside its budget under sustained load
  Given 5 accounts submitting at the per-UID limit for 1 hour
  Then the risk.evaluate span p95 is ≤5 ms throughout
  And the p95 in the final 10 minutes is within 20% of the first 10 minutes

Scenario: Kill-switch propagation budget
  Given the system under that load
  When the kill-switch is engaged
  Then the first server-side refusal occurs within 200 ms
  And every connected session has order affordances disabled within 2 s

Scenario (chaos): Restart does not unlock
  Given an active daily-loss lockout
  When the backend is restarted
  Then the lockout is still in force and the daily counter matches its pre-restart value within tolerance

Scenario (chaos): Failover never reports a false success
  Given a Postgres failover during engagement
  Then any account whose state write did not commit is reported in failures
  And no account is reported as frozen unless its state is durably written

Scenario (chaos): Clock skew does not release early
  Given the evaluator's wall clock jumps past the day boundary
  Then the lockout is not released and a clock-drift warning is raised on the system topic
```

## Technical notes / design
k6 runs against the demo environment from the same network position as the app (over Tailscale) so the measurement matches the budget's stated conditions (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §"Network conditions"), and the Bybit-RTT component is excluded from the backend-internal figure as that document specifies. The chaos harness uses container-level kill/restart and a Postgres failover fixture; each scenario asserts on both the API behaviour and the audit trail.

Clock skew is injected by faking the process clock while leaving the monotonic source intact, which is precisely the condition the `clock_drift` `SystemUpdate` kind exists to report (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9).

## Test plan
The deliverable is the test. Meta-assertions: each chaos scenario has a "control" run without the fault, proving the assertion can pass, so a scenario cannot pass because the fault never injected.

## Security notes
Chaos scenarios double as **availability abuse cases**: scenario 2 verifies that a crash cannot be used to clear the kill-switch, and scenario 3 that a failover cannot be used to produce a false "frozen" report that an operator would trust. Both are fail-closed properties, and their results are inputs to the E39-X02 review. Load tests run against demo only, never live, and use demo keys from the vault.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI under test here (affordance-disable timing is measured via the DOM but is a performance assertion, not an a11y one).

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: ≤5 ms p95 risk-gate contribution; ≤300 ms p95 order submit→ack on demo (budget #4, hard gate); ≤200 ms server-side halt; ≤2 s end-to-end kill-switch effectiveness; ≤500 ms breach→lockout notice. Any regression beyond the agreed threshold blocks the release per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2.

## Observability
Results are exported to the same Prometheus series used in production (`cv_risk_eval_duration_seconds`, `cv_kill_switch_engage_latency_seconds`, `cv_risk_breach_to_notice_seconds`) so the load-test numbers and the production numbers are directly comparable rather than living in separate reports.

- [ ] k6 script merged and run; results recorded against each budget.
- [ ] All six chaos scenarios implemented, each with a control run.

- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

title: Accessibility audit, exploratory charter and epic QA sign-off for E39
body:
## Context
Two DoD obligations close out E39. First, a11y: `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 states a11y is "default-on (WCAG 2.2 AA) for any ticket that ships or changes a UI surface, **including owner/admin screens** — there is no 'internal tool, a11y doesn't matter' exception", and the R3 a11y gate specifically requires that "danger/confirm patterns [are] announced" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4). Second, the epic-level QA sign-off: §2.2 requires "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA".

E39's screens are the product's danger surfaces, and a blocking `role="alert"` banner that traps focus, or a typed-confirmation dialog a screen-reader user cannot complete, would lock a user out of their own safety controls. That is the specific failure mode this ticket exists to prevent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Manual screen-reader passes** on SCR-071, SCR-072, SCR-073, SCR-134 and CMP-211 with **two** screen readers (NVDA on Windows and the Electron shell's platform reader), covering: the `role="alert"` lockout announcement; that the non-dismissible banner does **not** trap focus; the `role="alertdialog"` kill-switch flow end-to-end including typing `FREEZE`; the hold-to-confirm keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`) with `aria-valuenow` progress; the `aria-sort` account table; and SCR-134's per-limit fieldsets, units and breach descriptions.
- **Keyboard-only traversal**: complete a freeze, an unfreeze with step-up, a lockout override and a risk-policy save using only the keyboard, with visible focus at every step and no focus loss on modal open/close or on an async state change.
- **axe-core CI** configured for the four screens with zero violations at `serious`/`critical`; documented exceptions (if any) recorded with a rationale and a follow-up ticket.
- **Colour-independence and contrast verification**: greyscale rendering of every status state; contrast measurement of every status token pairing at ≥4.5:1 text / ≥3:1 non-text.
- **Exploratory charter** (session-based, 2×90 minutes): "Explore the risk and kill-switch surfaces with the mission of producing a state where the UI and the server disagree about whether trading is permitted" — plus a second charter targeting role transitions (a user's role or grant changes while a freeze dialog is open; `23-ws-protocol.md` §10 requires subscriptions to be re-authorised on kill-switch transitions and on grant changes, with `revoked` rather than silent emptying).
- **Epic-level regression pass** across E39's full scope on demo, and the recorded **QA sign-off** for the epic.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E automation (E39-Q02) and perf/chaos (E39-Q03).
- Visual/spec conformance (E39-D04 design QA).
- a11y of surfaces owned by other epics (order ticket, DOM ladder, rule editors) even though SCR-073 renders inside some of them — only the banner's behaviour in those hosts is in scope here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A screen-reader user can complete a freeze
  Given NVDA is active
  When the user opens the kill-switch modal via the global hotkey
  Then the dialog is announced as an alert dialog with its consequence text
  And focus starts on the cancel control
  And the user can type FREEZE, enter a reason and confirm without sighted assistance

Scenario: The lockout banner announces without trapping
  Given a lockout fires while the user is in the positions grid
  Then the banner is announced via role="alert"
  And keyboard focus remains where the user left it
  And the user can still reach and operate reduce-only controls

Scenario: Status is legible without colour
  Given every status state rendered in greyscale
  Then ok, WARN and LOCK remain distinguishable by text and glyph

Scenario (failure): A serious axe violation blocks sign-off
  Given axe-core reports a serious or critical violation on any E39 screen
  Then epic QA sign-off is withheld until it is fixed or a documented exception with a follow-up ticket exists

Scenario (exploratory): UI and server disagree
  Given the exploratory charter is executed
  Then any state where the UI permits an action the server refuses (or vice versa) is filed as a Bug with a reproduction
  And the absence of such a state is recorded explicitly as the charter's outcome
```

## Technical notes / design
axe-core runs in the Playwright suite from E39-Q02 against the same fixtures, so a11y checks exercise real states (locked, frozen, stale, partial failure) and not just an empty happy path — auditing only the default state is the most common way an a11y audit passes while the product remains unusable in its failure states.

Screen-reader sessions are recorded (screen + audio) and attached to the ticket, per the DoD's evidence expectations.

## Test plan
Manual + automated as described. The epic-level regression pass replays the E39-Q01 regression pack plus the E39-Q02 E2E suite against a fresh demo deployment and records pass/fail per scenario in the sign-off document.

## Security notes
The exploratory charter's central mission — producing a UI/server disagreement about whether trading is permitted — is simultaneously an a11y/UX charter and a **security** charter, because any such disagreement is a potential control bypass. Findings of that class route to E39-X02 and to the Security engineer immediately, not through the normal Bug queue. Recordings must not capture credentials or real account identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
The standard is WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. Specific gates for this epic: danger/confirm patterns announced; the node-canvas exception does not apply here (that is E37); every status text-labelled; meters expose numeric values; the hold-to-confirm gesture has a keyboard equivalent; no focus trap on non-dismissible banners.

## Performance notes
The audit confirms that assistive-technology usage does not push any surface outside its budget (e.g. the 1 Hz dashboard throttle must not cause the screen reader to re-announce the whole table each second — a real and commonly missed defect; the table uses `aria-live="off"` with targeted announcements instead).

## Observability
Findings are logged against the epic with severity; the sign-off document records pass/fail per scenario and is linked from the epic's DoD checklist.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Screen-reader passes completed on all four screens with two readers; recordings attached.
- [ ] Keyboard-only traversal completed for all four flows.
- [ ] axe-core green (no serious/critical) in CI on all E39 screens, exercising failure states.
- [ ] Greyscale and contrast verification recorded.
- [ ] Both exploratory charters executed, findings filed.

title: Enforce per-account risk caps server-side inside the order path
body:
## Context
**US-PROF-004 — Risk caps enforced server-side (Must)**: "As the owner, I want max position size, max daily loss and max concurrent positions enforced in the backend, so that limits survive a broken or hostile client." This story wires the M17 evaluator (E39-T01) into the OMS `Validator` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10) so that **every** order path — order ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule-engine action, trade-group fan-out leg, emulated-algo child — passes through the same check before any exchange call.

It also delivers the read surfaces the rest of the product needs to *show* headroom rather than discover it on rejection: `GET /api/v1/me/limits` (`EffectiveLimits`) and the server-side-scoped `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` (`RiskSummary`). US-POS-006's scoping NFR applies here — "the API never returns out-of-scope rows to a manager" — and `22-api-openapi.yaml` is explicit that a Viewer requesting an aggregate covering an account they cannot read gets `403 account_scope_denied` rather than a silently narrowed (and therefore misleading) number.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `RiskGate` integrated into the OMS `Validator` chain at `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/validator.py`, invoked **before** sizing and before any exchange call, for every command origin (`ticket`, `chart`, `dom`, `rule`, `fanout_leg`, `algo_child`). A test asserts the gate is unreachable-around: adding a new command origin without routing it through the gate fails a registry test.
- Error mapping to RFC 9457 problem responses using the existing catalogue in `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `risk_limit_breached` (422) with `detail` naming the cap, the limit and the current value; `account_locked`; `symbol_not_allowed`; and the new `risk_state_unavailable` (503) problem type added to the catalogue.
- `GET /api/v1/me/limits` returning `EffectiveLimits` — per-account `orders_per_minute_limit`/`used`, `rate_budget_pct_used`, `daily_loss_usd`/`daily_loss_cap_usd`, `open_positions`, `lockout_until` — so E30's order ticket can show remaining headroom before submission.
- `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` returning `RiskSummary` with `totals` (including `positions_without_native_stop`, surfaced from E32's invariant state) and per-account rows (`equity_usd`, `unrealised_pnl_usd`, `realised_pnl_today_usd`, `daily_loss_cap_usd`, `cap_utilisation_pct`, `open_positions`, `frozen`, `lockout`), with `accountIds` and `environment` query filters.
- Server-side scoping: Manager sees only granted accounts; Viewer gets the aggregate only when granted read on **every** covered account, else `403 account_scope_denied`.
- `risk_cap_usage` populated on the account-status WS payload (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15) so SCR-071 and the ticket's headroom chip update without polling.
- Audit: `risk_cap.changed` is emitted by the admin path (E39-S05); this story emits a structured audit entry for every *rejected* order with its cap, limit and actual value, so a hostile-client probe leaves a trail.

## Out of scope
- Automatic lockout creation on breach and the override flow (E39-S02) — this story refuses orders while a lockout exists but does not create one.
- Kill-switch state (E39-S03); the gate consumes it through a port with a stub until S03 lands.
- Any UI (E39-S04, E39-S05).
- Rate-limit budgeting against Bybit's per-UID limits (E34) — `max_orders_per_minute` here is a **user-configured risk cap**, not exchange rate budgeting, and the two are deliberately separate counters.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Position size cap rejects before any exchange call
  Given account C caps position size at 0.5 BTC and holds 0.4 BTC
  When an order for 0.2 BTC is submitted
  Then the response is 422 with code risk_limit_breached
  And the detail reads "would exceed max position 0.5 BTC (current 0.4)"
  And no request was made to Bybit
  And an audit entry records the rejection

Scenario: Concurrent positions cap still permits reduce-only
  Given the cap is 3 and 3 positions are open
  When an order that would open a fourth symbol is submitted
  Then it is rejected with risk_limit_breached
  When a reduce-only order on an existing position is submitted
  Then it is accepted

Scenario: Every path is gated
  Given the kill-switch is released and caps are exceeded
  When an order is attempted from the ticket, a chart drag, a DOM click, a rule action, a fan-out leg and an emulated-algo child
  Then all six are rejected with the same code and the same message
  And each rejection is audited with its origin

Scenario: Manager scoping on the risk summary
  Given manager M is granted accounts A and B only
  When M calls GET /api/v1/risk/summary without filters
  Then only A and B appear and no filter value can reveal account C

Scenario (failure): Viewer requesting an unreadable aggregate
  Given a viewer lacks read on one account covered by the requested aggregate
  When GET /api/v1/risk/summary is called
  Then the response is 403 account_scope_denied
  And no partial aggregate is returned

Scenario (edge): Risk state unavailable
  Given the risk service cannot produce fresh state for account C
  When an opening order for C is submitted
  Then it is rejected with 503 risk_state_unavailable
  And GET /api/v1/risk/summary marks account C as stale
```

## Technical notes / design
The gate is a dependency in the FastAPI order router's chain (`session -> scope -> rate limit -> validate`, `20-architecture.md` §3.12) and *also* a direct call inside `OrderService.submit`, so a future internal caller that bypasses HTTP still cannot bypass the gate. The registry test enumerates `OrderCommand.origin` values and asserts each has a gated code path.

`EffectiveLimits` and `RiskSummary` are assembled from the in-memory `RiskService` counters plus a single indexed lockout probe — no per-request aggregation query over `executions`, which would blow the latency budget.

`positions_without_native_stop` is read from E32's invariant tracker; until E32 lands it reports from the OMS position state with a `null`-free default of 0 and a feature flag `risk.native_stop_surfacing` gating the banner. Documented so E32 can flip it on without a schema change.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: gate wiring (each origin), error mapping (each code → status + problem body), scoping predicate (owner/manager/viewer × granted/ungranted).
- **Contract**: OpenAPI schemathesis run over `/me/limits`, `/risk/summary`, and the new `risk_state_unavailable` problem type; response bodies validate against `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Integration**: recorded Bybit demo fixtures driving PnL across the daily-loss cap and position count across the concurrent-positions cap; assert no outbound exchange call occurs on a rejected order (HTTP mock asserts zero calls).
- **E2E**: covered by E39-Q02 (every path under caps).
- **Perf**: k6 profile submitting at the per-UID limit; assert added p95 ≤5 ms and total order submit → ack p95 <300 ms on demo.
- **Security**: abuse-case tests in E39-X02; this story includes a negative test that a client-supplied `risk_caps` field in an order body is ignored.
- Coverage: ≥90 % on touched M17 and validator code.

## Security notes
Directly implements the mitigation for `04-security-program.md` threat class "tampering — client-side cap bypass" and P8 server-side authority. Abuse cases covered by tests here: submitting caps in the request body; submitting with a forged account id outside scope; probing another account's existence through `/risk/summary` filters (must return the same 403 shape whether the account exists or not — no enumeration). Data classification: financial state and account identifiers; no secrets in responses or logs. `security` label mandatory per DoD §8 (any ticket touching `area/oms-execution` order-placement paths).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend only. The error `detail` strings are user-visible copy, so they are reviewed against the E39-D01 copy deck and must be full sentences naming the cap, not codes.

## Performance notes
≤5 ms p95 added to the order path (US-PROF-004 and US-ADMIN-003 NFRs); inside budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2, hard gate for R3 demo). `/risk/summary` responds within 400 ms p95 for up to 20 accounts; `risk_cap_usage` is delivered on the existing account-status WS cadence and adds no new topic.

## Observability
Metrics from E39-T01 plus `cv_risk_gate_rejections_total{origin,code}` and `cv_risk_summary_duration_seconds`. Every rejection logs `request_id`, origin, account, cap, limit, actual. Audit entries for rejections use action `order.rejected` with a `risk` reason payload. Grafana "Risk & safety" panel gains a rejection-by-origin breakdown.

title: Automatic lockout on cap breach with day-boundary reset and step-up override
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the automatic-lockout, day-boundary reset and step-up override lifecycle (clear→warning→locked) is built directly on the library via the factory; the day-boundary timer and override window are the chart's coarse `after:` states, not hand-rolled bookkeeping.

**US-RULE-012 — Daily loss limit and lockout (Must)**: "As the owner, I want automatic flatten and lockout at a daily loss threshold, so that a bad day cannot become a disaster." Where E39-S01 refuses individual orders, this story adds the **state machine**: a breach transitions the account into a persisted lockout, which cancels working orders (and optionally flattens per policy), blocks new entries while leaving reduce-only available, pushes the state to every affected session, resets at the configured day boundary, and can be cleared early only by the owner with step-up re-authentication and a mandatory audited reason.

The API contract already exists: `POST /api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override` — "Lockouts are set automatically when a `RiskCaps` threshold is breached. Clearing one is an owner-only, step-up-gated, always-audited action; the reason is mandatory and is written to the audit chain" (`22-api-openapi.yaml`). `04-security-program.md` SR-025 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §12 both list clearing a risk lockout among step-up-required actions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the `B20` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B20.risk_lockout.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('risk_lockout', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b20_risk_lockout.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b20_risk_lockout.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- `LockoutService` in `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/lockout.py`: on a breach detected by the evaluation cycle (event-driven on every position/execution event, plus a timer at `risk.eval_interval_seconds` = 5 s per the US-RULE-012 NFR), open a `risk_lockouts` row with `reason` ∈ {`daily_loss`, `consecutive_losses`, `max_positions`, `manual`}, `threshold`, `actual_value`, `since`, `until`.
- **Breach behaviour driven by `risk_policy.breach_behaviour`** per limit (`warn` | `block` | `flatten`), per the SCR-134 design: `warn` raises an alert only; `block` cancels working orders and refuses new entries; `flatten` additionally issues reduce-only closes via the OMS and records `risk.auto_flatten`. Defaults are conservative (`block` for daily loss).
- Idempotency: a breach that persists across evaluation cycles must not open a second lockout or re-cancel orders — enforced by the partial unique index from E39-T02 and an explicit "already locked" fast path.
- **Day-boundary reset**: the lockout auto-releases at the configured boundary (`risk_policy.day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes`, default UTC per `24-internal-schemas.md` §11); the reset time is exposed in the API and shown on SCR-073.
- **Override**: `POST /api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override` — owner only (`killswitch:write`), step-up token required (`elevated_until` valid), mandatory `reason` (3..280 chars per the schema; the SCR-071 UI additionally requires ≥10 characters), idempotency key required. On success the lockout is released with a **shortened override window** (US-RULE-012: "a shortened override window is applied") after which the cap re-arms — window length configurable, default 60 minutes.
- Audit: `risk.lockout_triggered` `{scope, rule, threshold, actualValue, accountIds}`, `risk.lockout_overridden` (**high severity**), `risk.auto_flatten`, `risk.lockout_acknowledged` — the exact action names from the SCR-073 catalogue entry and `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.
- WS push: a `system` frame (`SystemUpdate`, `kind: "notice"`, `severity: "critical"`) within 500 ms of the breach so SCR-073 appears without a poll; plus the account-status `lockout` field so SCR-071 rows flip to LOCK.
- Manager **override request** path: a manager cannot clear their own lockout; the request notifies the owner (via E40's channels when available, and always via the in-app notice) and the attempt is audited.

## Out of scope
- The lockout UI (E39-S04) and the freeze/kill-switch UI (E39-S05).
- Rule-engine-authored risk rules and the dead man's switch, US-RULE-013 (E35).
- Flatten-all as a manual panic action (E29 endpoint; E39-T03 runbook) — here flatten is only the automatic, policy-driven variant.
- Notification delivery channels (E40); this story emits the events they consume.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Threshold breached
  Given account C has max_daily_loss_usd 1500
  When realised+unrealised PnL reaches -1500
  Then a risk_lockouts row is opened with reason daily_loss, threshold 1500 and the actual value
  And working orders are cancelled per the configured breach behaviour
  And order placement for C is disabled while reduce-only remains available
  And every session scoped to C receives a system WS frame within 500 ms
  And risk.lockout_triggered is audited

Scenario: Owner override requires step-up
  Given account C is locked out
  When the owner calls the override endpoint without a valid step-up token
  Then the response is 403 and no lockout is released
  When the owner repeats with a valid step-up token and a 12-character reason
  Then the lockout is released, a shortened override window is applied
  And risk.lockout_overridden is audited at high severity with the reason

Scenario: Boundary reset
  Given a lockout with reason daily_loss and no explicit until
  When the configured day boundary passes
  Then the lockout is released automatically, the daily counter resets, and the reset is audited

Scenario (failure): Manager attempts self-override
  Given manager M is locked out on their granted account
  When M calls the override endpoint
  Then the response is 403
  And the attempt is audited
  And the owner is notified of the override request

Scenario (edge): Breach persists across cycles
  Given a lockout is already active for the breached cap
  When the next evaluation cycle observes the same breach
  Then no second lockout row is created and no orders are cancelled a second time

Scenario (edge): Breach during backend restart
  Given the backend restarts while a lockout is active
  When it comes back up
  Then the lockout is still in force (it is persisted, not in-memory)
  And accounts are not silently unlocked by the restart
```

## Technical notes / design

**Statechart contract.** Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B20.1–.8. Mandatory config: `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §1.2 (`79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §3 stay plain code.
Evaluation is driven by the `oms.*` event bus (immediate) and a 5 s ticker (safety net), both calling the same `LockoutService.evaluate(account)` so there is one code path. Cancellation of working orders reuses the OMS cancel-all path with a `reason=risk_lockout` tag so the audit trail attributes it correctly rather than looking like a user cancel.

The override's "shortened window" is implemented as a new `risk_lockouts` row with `reason='manual'` and `until = now + override_window_minutes` marked `released_at` NULL but non-blocking — i.e. it is a *grace* record used to re-arm the cap — documented in `24-internal-schemas.md` so the semantics are not inferred from code.

Config keys: `risk.eval_interval_seconds` (5), `risk.override_window_minutes` (60), `risk.lockout_default_minutes` (from `risk_policy.lockout_minutes_default`, bounded 0..1440).

## Test plan

**Statechart test plan additions:**
- Pure-API unit tests of the `b20_risk_lockout` binding module using a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership in `tests/xstate_contract/test_b20_risk_lockout.py`, covering both spellings and every §B20.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point this ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a `machine_hash` or HMAC mismatch.
- **Unit**: breach detection per reason; idempotency (repeat cycles); day-boundary release arithmetic; override token validation; shortened-window re-arm; manager self-override refusal.
- **Contract**: `POST /risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override` request/response and 403 shapes against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the `SystemUpdate` frame validates against the `cv://ws/v1/system.schema.json` schema in `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9.
- **Integration**: recorded fixture where partial fills walk PnL to the threshold; assert cancellation set, audit rows and WS frame ordering.
- **Chaos** (with E39-Q03): backend restart mid-lockout; Postgres failover during breach handling; WS disconnect between breach and push (client must still see the lockout on reconnect via the snapshot, not only the delta).
- **E2E**: in E39-Q02.
- Coverage ≥90 % on the lockout package.

## Security notes
Threats: elevation of privilege (self-override, manager clearing another's lockout), repudiation (unaudited release), tampering (client-supplied `until`). Controls: owner-only `killswitch:write`, SR-025 step-up, mandatory audited reason, server-computed `until` (never accepted from the client), and idempotency keys to prevent replayed overrides. Every override is `high` severity in the audit chain so E42's browser surfaces it prominently. Data classification: financial + accountability data; retained indefinitely. `security` label mandatory.

## Accessibility notes
Backend, but the copy it emits is rendered by `role="alert"` surfaces: the lockout reason string must be a full sentence naming the breached limit, the actual value and the reset time (SCR-073 requires all three), never a bare code. Reason strings come from the E39-D01 copy deck.

## Performance notes
Lockout probe on the order path is an index-only lookup within the ≤5 ms evaluator budget. Breach → WS notice ≤500 ms (SCR-073 performance note). The 5 s ticker must not exceed the reconciliation rate budget (US-POS-008 NFR) — it reads in-memory counters, issuing no extra exchange calls.

## Observability
`cv_risk_lockouts_active` gauge (labels: reason), `cv_risk_lockout_transitions_total{reason,transition}`, `cv_risk_override_total{outcome}`, `cv_risk_breach_to_notice_seconds` histogram (asserted against the 500 ms budget). Audit actions as listed. Alert rule: any `risk.lockout_overridden` pages the owner.

## Definition of Done

**Statechart DoD additions:** `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90 %; CI green.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` reflect the shipped override and grace semantics.
- [ ] Chaos scenarios (restart, failover) pass.
- [ ] Security review: step-up enforcement and audit completeness manually abuse-tested.
- [ ] QA sign-off per the E39-Q01 plan.
- [ ] Demoed: a simulated loss sequence drives a lockout and an owner override at Sprint Review.
