title: Kill-switch engine: global and scoped freeze over REST with WS propagation
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the KillSwitch engine (states clear→engaging→engaged/error, C-07b unguarded RELEASE fall-through) is built directly on the library via the factory; the enum, transition table and snapshot/rehydrate code it replaces are dropped.

**US-RULE-014 — Owner kill-switch (Must)**: "As the owner, I want to freeze a manager or everything instantly, so that I can stop harm immediately," with the NFR "freeze is enforced at the API boundary, not in the UI; effective within 2 s". The roadmap fixes the semantics (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E39 row): the kill-switch halts "all new order placement, all rule-engine actions and all fan-out across all accounts… with the semantics **'stops new risk, does not force-close'**".

The contract is already written in `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET|POST /api/v1/trading/kill-switch`. Engaging "(a) refuses all new order/amend requests with `trading_disabled`, (b) optionally cancels all open orders, (c) optionally flattens all positions with reduce-only market orders, and (d) disarms every `armed` rule". Managers may engage it for accounts in their own scope; **only the owner may engage it globally or release it**. Bybit's own dead-man's-switch (`POST /v5/order/disconnected-cancel-all`) is `inverse`-only, so the local kill-switch is the operative control for USDT linear perps.

R3 exit criterion 7 (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3) is this story's bar: "Kill-switch works end-to-end: activated, no new order can be placed by any path including the rule engine; existing positions untouched; released cleanly; every transition audited."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the `B18` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B18.kill_switch.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('kill_switch', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b18_kill_switch.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b18_kill_switch.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- `KillSwitchService` in `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/killswitch.py` backed by `kill_switch_state` (E39-T02), with a **fail-closed** cached read (≤5 s staleness; unreadable state ⇒ trading refused) matching the `feature_flags.is_killswitch` re-read rule in `21-database-schema.md` §3.9.
- `GET /api/v1/trading/kill-switch` → `KillSwitch` (`engaged`, `scope`, `exchange_account_ids`, `engaged_at`, `engaged_by`, `reason`).
- `POST /api/v1/trading/kill-switch` accepting `SetKillSwitchRequest` (`engaged`, `scope` ∈ {`global`,`accounts`}, `exchange_account_ids`, `cancel_open_orders` default true, `flatten_positions` **default false**, `disarm_rules` default true, `reason` 3..280) with a **required idempotency key**, returning `KillSwitchResult` with per-account `actions` counts and a `failures` array.
- Enforcement: the gate from E39-S01 consults kill-switch state first; every order/amend path returns `trading_disabled`; fan-out legs report `kill_switch_engaged` (the enum value already present in `TradeGroupPreview.legs[].rejection.code`); the rule runtime is disarmed via the `rules` integration point so rule actions cannot fire (US-RULE-011's safety-override precedence: "a risk control always wins, regardless of configured priority").
- **Positions untouched by default** — `flatten_positions` defaults to false and is only honoured when explicitly true; a test asserts that a default-options engagement closes nothing.
- RBAC: `killswitch:write`; scope `granted_accounts` for a manager engaging within scope; **owner-only** for `scope: global` and for **any** release, enforced server-side with a test per role × scope × direction.
- Step-up: releasing the kill-switch requires a valid step-up token (SR-025 explicitly lists "disabling the kill switch").
- Propagation: a `system` WS frame (`SystemUpdate`, `kind: "kill_switch"`, with the `actions` counts) to every connection — `system` is auto-subscribed and cannot be unsubscribed (`23-ws-protocol.md` §9), so no client can miss it; affected private subscriptions are re-authorised per §10 ("Authorisation is re-evaluated… on kill-switch transitions").
- Partial-failure semantics: a per-account failure (REST timeout, exchange 5xx) is reported in `failures` with a retryable error, does not roll back successful accounts, and leaves the switch engaged.
- Audit: one record per affected entity (US-RULE-014: "one audit record per affected entity"), actions `risk.freeze` (with the full option set) and `risk.unfreeze`; `user_account_access.frozen`/`frozen_at`/`frozen_by`/`frozen_reason` maintained for per-manager freezes.
- Global-hotkey server contract: the hotkey opens the confirmation UI (E39-S05); the backend exposes no unconfirmed one-shot endpoint — engagement always carries a typed reason.

## Out of scope
- The confirmation modal, panic cluster and hotkey binding (E39-S05).
- `POST /positions/close-all` implementation (E29); this story calls it when `flatten_positions` is true.
- Bybit DCP arming for `inverse` instruments — out of scope product-wide (USDT linear perps only).
- The feature-flag console surface of the kill-switch (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Global engagement stops new risk within 2 seconds
  Given open positions and 4 armed rules across 5 accounts
  When the owner engages the kill-switch with scope global and default options
  Then within 2 seconds every order and amend request is refused with trading_disabled
  And all 4 rules are disarmed
  And zero positions are closed
  And open orders are cancelled because cancel_open_orders defaults to true
  And one audit record exists per affected entity

Scenario: Manager may freeze only their own scope
  Given manager M is granted account A only
  When M engages the kill-switch with scope accounts for A
  Then it succeeds
  When M attempts scope global, or scope accounts including account B
  Then the response is 403 and no state changes

Scenario: Release requires owner plus step-up
  Given the kill-switch is engaged globally
  When a manager attempts to release it
  Then the response is 403
  When the owner attempts release without a step-up token
  Then the response is 403
  When the owner releases with a valid step-up token and a reason
  Then the switch is released, rules remain disarmed until explicitly re-armed, and risk.unfreeze is audited

Scenario (failure): One account fails during engagement
  Given account C's REST path times out while cancelling orders
  When the owner engages the kill-switch across 5 accounts
  Then the switch is engaged, the other 4 accounts report their action counts
  And failures contains account C with a retryable error
  And nothing is rolled back

Scenario (edge): Fail-closed on unreadable state
  Given the kill_switch_state read fails
  When an order is submitted
  Then it is refused, never admitted optimistically

Scenario (edge): Idempotent re-engagement
  Given the switch is already engaged globally
  When the same request is replayed with the same idempotency key
  Then the stored result is returned and no orders are cancelled a second time
```

## Technical notes / design

**Statechart contract.** Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B18.1–.8. Mandatory config: `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §1.2 (`79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §3 stay plain code.
Engagement is ordered **refuse-first**: the state row is written and the cache invalidated *before* any cancellation or flatten work begins, so the 200 ms server-side halt (SCR-072 performance note) does not wait on exchange round-trips. Cancellation/flatten/disarm then run concurrently per account with per-account results streamed into `KillSwitchResult.failures`.

Rule disarming goes through the rule-engine port (`rule.kill_switched` audit action already defined in `24-internal-schemas.md` §12) rather than writing rule tables directly, so E35 owns its own invariants.

Idempotency reuses the OMS idempotency store keyed on the required `Idempotency-Key` header, storing the `KillSwitchResult` so a replay is byte-identical.

Config keys: `risk.killswitch_cache_max_age_seconds` (5), `risk.killswitch_action_concurrency` (per-account parallelism), `risk.killswitch_action_timeout_seconds`.

## Test plan

**Statechart test plan additions:**
- Pure-API unit tests of the `b18_kill_switch` binding module using a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership in `tests/xstate_contract/test_b18_kill_switch.py`, covering both spellings and every §B18.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point this ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a `machine_hash` or HMAC mismatch.
- **Unit**: state transitions, RBAC matrix (owner/manager/viewer × global/accounts × engage/release), option handling (each of the three flags independently), fail-closed read, idempotent replay.
- **Contract**: `KillSwitch`, `SetKillSwitchRequest`, `KillSwitchResult` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the `kind: "kill_switch"` frame against `cv://ws/v1/system.schema.json`.
- **Integration**: recorded fixtures with an injected 5xx and an injected timeout on one account, asserting partial-failure reporting and no rollback.
- **E2E** (E39-Q02): every order-placement path attempted while engaged, including a rule action and a fan-out leg — zero escapes, matching R3 exit criterion 7.
- **Perf**: measure engagement → first refusal (target ≤200 ms server-side) and engagement → WS frame at the client (target ≤2 s) under a loaded system.
- **Chaos** (E39-Q03): backend restart while engaged (must come back engaged); Postgres failover during engagement.
- Coverage ≥90 %.

## Security notes
This is the highest-value target in the product: an attacker who can *disable* the kill-switch removes the last safety control (`04-security-program.md` §5 threat D2 — "Feature-flag screen used to enable live trading without review", mitigated by SR-025 step-up on kill-switch disable). Controls implemented here: owner-only release, step-up token, mandatory audited reason, idempotency to block replay, fail-closed reads, and one audit row per affected entity so a partial or forged action is detectable. A manager engaging outside scope and any release attempt by a non-owner are logged as security events, not just 403s. Abuse cases are exercised in E39-X02.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The `reason` and per-account failure messages are rendered in `role="alertdialog"` content, so they must be plain sentences (copy deck from E39-D01), and the action counts must render meaningfully at zero.

## Performance notes
Server-side halt within 200 ms of the backend call (SCR-072); effective within 2 s end-to-end including WS propagation (US-RULE-014 NFR). The cached state read adds <0.5 ms to the order path, inside the ≤5 ms risk budget and budget #4.

## Observability
`cv_kill_switch_engaged` gauge (0/1, labelled by scope), `cv_kill_switch_transitions_total{scope,direction,actor_role}`, `cv_kill_switch_action_failures_total{action}`, `cv_kill_switch_engage_latency_seconds` histogram. Audit: `risk.freeze`, `risk.unfreeze`, `rule.kill_switched`, `position.flattened` (when opted in). Alerting: `cv_kill_switch_engaged == 1` pages immediately; a failure entry in `failures` raises a warning alert.

## Definition of Done

**Statechart DoD additions:** `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

title: Build the risk dashboard SCR-071 and the lockout notice SCR-073
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-004 — Owner risk dashboard (Must)**: "As the owner, I want an aggregate risk view across all accounts, so that I can supervise at a glance," and the user-facing half of **US-RULE-012** (the lockout banner with its expiry) and **US-PROF-004** (cap utilisation made visible before it is breached). The backend for both landed in E39-S01 and E39-S02; this story builds the surfaces: **SCR-071 Risk dashboard** at route `/risk`, and **SCR-073 Lockout notice**, the blocking banner a manager sees when trading is halted.

Design is signed off in E39-D02 (Sprint 14), satisfying the design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`: "no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off").

The story is deliberately 8 points and covers two screens because they share one data source (`RiskSummary` plus the account-status WS payload) and two components (CMP-117, CMP-138); splitting them would duplicate the data layer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/risk` (`12-sitemap.md`), RBAC-gated: `owner` full; `manager` sees only their granted scope; `viewer` read-only when granted — scoping is displayed, but **enforced server-side** (E39-S01); the client never filters for security.
- **SCR-071** implementation per the catalogue: portfolio header (equity, uPnL, day P&L, drawdown), exposure by symbol with % of equity, and the per-account table (`account`, `equity`, `day P&L`, `cap`, `used`, `positions`, `state`) driven by `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` plus live updates from the `system` topic and the account-status `risk_cap_usage` field.
- Control row: **FREEZE per account**, **FREEZE ALL**, and **Override lockout** — each opening the shared confirmation surfaces owned by E39-S05 (this story renders the entry points and wires the callbacks; the modal itself is S05's deliverable, consumed here as a component).
- The **critical banner** when `RiskSummary.totals.positions_without_native_stop > 0` — the OpenAPI schema states this "MUST be zero in steady state; any non-zero value is a violation of the native-stop safety invariant and is surfaced as a critical banner."
- All SCR-071 states: normal · warning (≥80 % of a cap) · locked (showing what was auto-flattened and when) · frozen · stale data (per-account freshness timestamp; every figure carries one per the US-ADMIN-004 NFR) · reconciling after reconnect · manager-scoped · viewer read-only · empty (no accounts).
- **SCR-073** implementation: the non-dismissible blocking banner + panel state — "Trading locked: daily loss limit −2 % reached at 13:41 UTC. 1 position was flattened. Locked until 00:00 UTC. Contact the owner for an override." — rendered consistently in the order ticket, the positions grid and the risk dashboard (the catalogue requires it to appear in all three); the manager override-request action; the countdown to reset (CMP-035); post-expiry clearing.
- Components built/consumed: **CMP-117 RiskLockoutBanner** and **CMP-138 RiskCapMeter** implemented to their catalogue contracts with Storybook stories for every variant; plus CMP-049 Table, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-028 Callout, CMP-035 Countdown.
- Client state: a `useRiskSummary` hook merging the REST snapshot with `system` deltas, with reconnect-safe resubscription (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11 restore order) and an explicit stale marker rather than a frozen-but-plausible number.

## Out of scope
- SCR-072 kill-switch modal, CMP-211 panic cluster, the global hotkey and SCR-134 (E39-S05).
- The positions/orders grid itself (E29) — this story only ensures SCR-073 renders inside it via a shared banner slot.
- Journal equity-curve analytics (E41); CMP-167 is consumed with the data `RiskSummary` already provides.
- Notification delivery (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Aggregate view
  Given the owner opens /risk with three accounts
  Then equity, exposure, uPnL, daily PnL, drawdown, margin usage and liquidation proximity are shown per account and in aggregate
  And every figure displays a freshness timestamp

Scenario: Threshold breach escalates with text, not colour alone
  Given account sub_001 crosses 80% of its daily-loss cap
  Then its row shows WARN as text plus a glyph and its RiskCapMeter shows the numeric current and cap values
  And the row remains distinguishable when rendered in greyscale

Scenario: Lockout notice appears within 500 ms and cannot be dismissed
  Given a manager is trading and their account breaches its daily-loss cap
  When the system WS frame arrives
  Then SCR-073 appears within 500 ms with role="alert"
  And it names the reason, the breached limit, the actual value and the reset time
  And no dismiss affordance exists while the lockout holds
  And it is visible in the order ticket, the positions grid and the risk dashboard

Scenario: Manager sees only their scope
  Given manager M is granted accounts A and B
  When M opens /risk
  Then only A and B appear and no control can reveal account C

Scenario (failure): One account's feed is down
  Given account sub_002's data is stale beyond the freshness threshold
  Then its row renders an explicit "stale" state with its last-known timestamp
  And its figures are not presented as current

Scenario (edge): Native-stop invariant violated
  Given RiskSummary.totals.positions_without_native_stop is 2
  Then a critical banner is shown naming the count and linking to the affected positions

Scenario (edge): Reconnect
  Given the WS disconnects and reconnects
  Then the dashboard re-fetches the snapshot, resubscribes, and clears the reconciling state without a full page reload
```

## Technical notes / design
Code lives in `apps/web/src/features/risk/`. Data flow: `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` for the snapshot → `system` topic deltas (auto-subscribed, cannot be unsubscribed) → per-account status updates. Updates are throttled to **1 Hz** at the view layer (SCR-071 performance note) even though events may arrive faster; the throttle is in the hook, not in each component, so counts and meters never disagree within a frame.

SCR-073 is rendered from a single `LockoutBannerSlot` provider so all three host surfaces show identical copy; the state is **server-derived** (`RiskSummary.accounts[].lockout`) and persists across reloads — the catalogue explicitly forbids a client-derived lockout.

FREEZE / FREEZE ALL / Override entry points are disabled-with-reason for roles lacking `killswitch:write`; disabled state includes an accessible explanation, not a bare disabled attribute.

## Test plan
- **Unit (Vitest)**: the `useRiskSummary` merge/throttle logic; stale detection; cap-utilisation formatting; countdown arithmetic across the day boundary; role-based control enablement.
- **Component (Storybook + interaction tests)**: every CMP-117 and CMP-138 variant; SCR-071 in all nine states; SCR-073 in all four states.
- **Contract**: MSW handlers generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` so the UI cannot drift from `RiskSummary`.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron)**: breach → lockout appears in all three surfaces → override by owner → banner clears; manager scoping; reconnect behaviour. (Shared suite maintained in E39-Q02.)

title: Build the kill-switch modal SCR-072, panic cluster, global hotkey and risk policy SCR-134
body:
## Context
The operator-facing half of the kill-switch (**US-RULE-014**) and of risk administration (**US-ADMIN-003 — Risk-limit administration, Must**). The backend landed in E39-S03 and E39-S01; this story ships the controls: **SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation modal**, the **CMP-211 PanicButtons** cluster that lives permanently in the app shell (SCR-010), the **global hotkey** the roadmap requires ("flippable from the admin screen and from a global hotkey", `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2), and **SCR-134 Admin: risk policy (global)** at `/admin/risk-policy`.

This is the most consequence-dense UI in the product. The catalogue's requirements for SCR-072 are non-negotiable: name exactly which accounts and users are affected; restate the consequence in text; one blast-radius Confirm whose button names the effect (no typed word, no hold, no step-up — architect ruling on #829, 2026-10-14); offer "also cancel working orders" (default **on**, the API default) and "also flatten positions" (default **off**) as explicit checkboxes; `role="alertdialog"` with **focus starting on the cancel control**.

Design is signed off in E39-D03 (Sprint 14) per the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-072** modal: scope selector (this account / all accounts; per-symbol scope is not in the API — OD-7 in `docs/design/E39/E39-D01.md`; a mixed-environment account set is refused and global covers every environment, D-3; a Manager engages within grants only, never `flatten_positions`, D-1); a live consequence restatement computed from `RiskSummary` ("This cancels 14 working orders and blocks new orders on 5 accounts. Open positions are NOT closed."); the two opt-in checkboxes mapping to `cancel_open_orders` and `flatten_positions` (flatten implies cancel: ticking flatten sets cancel on and disables it with a reason, because B18 first enters `flattening` from `cancelling.onDone`); the mandatory `reason` field (3..280); single blast-radius confirm (`variant="standard"`, label names the effect, `reason` pre-filled and editable) via CMP-044 `variant="standard"`; execution state with per-account progress; the completed summary rendered from `KillSwitchResult.actions`; partial failure with per-account retry that does not re-execute succeeded accounts; the **unfreeze** path with its own confirmation and step-up; DEMO vs LIVE variants.
- **CMP-211 PanicButtons**: Flatten-all / Cancel-all / Kill-switch cluster with `scope: account|group|global`, `confirmMode: hold|typed|single`, RBAC-driven `enabled` map, and hold-confirm progress exposed via `aria-valuenow` with a keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`). Wired to `POST /positions/close-all`, `POST /orders/cancel-all` and `POST /trading/kill-switch`, every invocation wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- **Global hotkey**: a binding registered in the hotkey system that **opens SCR-072** — it never fires a freeze directly. Discoverable in the hotkey cheatsheet (SCR-013). Deliberately distinct from the environment switcher, which the catalogue states is intentionally not bindable.
- **SCR-134** admin page at `/admin/risk-policy`: every global limit with units (max daily loss, max drawdown, max total notional, max positions, max leverage, max orders/min, per-symbol concentration), the per-limit breach-behaviour selector (warn / block new orders / flatten), the current measured value beside each limit, lockout durations, override policy, freeze defaults, and the "block trading while the backend is degraded" switch; validation that portfolio caps are ≥ the sum of the smallest per-account caps with an explanatory warning; the "this cannot be disabled entirely" guard; a change summary before save; **step-up gate on save** (SR-025); `risk_policy.updated` audited.
- Per-manager limit editing surface on SCR-122 (Admin: user detail) for US-ADMIN-003's per-manager caps, with the tighten-during-open-position semantics: no forced liquidation, new entries blocked, reduce-only preserved, both owner and manager informed, and every change audited with old and new values.
- Optimistic-UI prohibition: none of these controls shows success before the server acknowledges (SCR-134 performance note: "the screen confirms only after the server acknowledges").

## Out of scope
- SCR-071 / SCR-073 (E39-S04).
- The backend kill-switch engine (E39-S03) and cap enforcement (E39-S01).
- The feature-flag console (E42) and live-enablement gate (E44), both of which embed but do not own these controls.
- The flatten-all runbook document (E39-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Freeze with safe defaults
  Given the owner opens the kill-switch modal for all accounts
  Then "also flatten positions" is unchecked
  And "also cancel working orders" reflects the API default (checked), stated explicitly in the consequence text
  And the consequence text states that open positions are NOT closed
  And focus is on the cancel control
  And the confirm action is reached by Tab and activated by Enter with the pre-filled reason; no typed word is required

Scenario: Flatten implies cancel
  Given the owner opens the kill-switch modal
  When the owner ticks "also flatten positions"
  Then "also cancel working orders" is checked and disabled with the reason "Closing at market requires cancelling working orders first — a resting entry could re-open exposure"
  And the request never carries flatten_positions true with cancel_open_orders false

Scenario: Execution and completion summary
  Given the owner confirms a global freeze across 5 accounts
  Then per-account progress is shown as results arrive
  And the completed summary shows orders_cancelled, positions_flattened and rules_disarmed from KillSwitchResult
  And zero counts render as meaningful text rather than a blank

Scenario: Partial failure with retry
  Given account C failed during the freeze
  Then a partial-failure state names account C and its error
  And retry re-attempts only account C
  And the switch remains engaged throughout

Scenario: Unfreeze requires step-up
  Given the kill-switch is engaged
  When the owner chooses unfreeze
  Then a step-up authentication challenge is presented
  And on success the modal states that rules remain disarmed until explicitly re-armed

Scenario: Hotkey never fires directly
  Given the global kill-switch hotkey is pressed
  Then SCR-072 opens with the confirmation requirements intact
  And no request is sent until the user confirms

Scenario (failure): Saving a conflicting risk policy
  Given a portfolio cap lower than the sum of the smallest per-account caps
  When the owner saves SCR-134
  Then an explanatory warning names the conflicting caps
  And the save is blocked until resolved or explicitly acknowledged per the design

Scenario (edge): Tightening a limit below current exposure
  Given a manager holds exposure exceeding a newly tightened limit
  When the owner saves the tighter limit with step-up
  Then the UI states that no position will be force-closed, new entries are blocked and reduce-only remains available
  And both owner and manager see the change
  And the audit entry records old and new values

Scenario (edge): Viewer role
  Given a viewer opens the app shell
  Then the panic cluster renders disabled with an accessible explanation
  And forcing the control client-side still results in a 403 from the server
```

## Technical notes / design
Code in `apps/web/src/features/risk/killswitch/` and `apps/web/src/features/admin/risk-policy/`. The consequence text is computed from a live `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` fetched when the modal opens — never from cached counts that could be minutes old — and re-fetched if the modal stays open beyond 30 s, because presenting a stale "14 working orders" is a correctness bug in a danger dialog.

Every mutating call sends a required `Idempotency-Key`; retry after a partial failure reuses a **new** key scoped to the retried accounts, so a retry cannot replay the whole engagement.

The hotkey is registered through the existing hotkey profile system (`hotkey_profiles` table, `GET /me/keymap`) so it is rebindable and appears in the cheatsheet; it is registered with a guard so it cannot fire while a modal already has focus.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: confirmation gating (reason present, 3..280; no typed word; flatten disabled for a Manager, D-1); checkbox→request-field mapping (flatten ticked ⇒ cancel on and locked; never `flatten_positions: true` with `cancel_open_orders: false`); consequence-text computation including pluralisation and zero cases; retry key scoping; SCR-134 validation rules; role-based enablement.
- **Component (Storybook + interaction tests)**: every SCR-072 state and every CMP-211 variant; keyboard hold-confirm; DEMO vs LIVE variants.
- **Contract**: MSW handlers generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` for `SetKillSwitchRequest`/`KillSwitchResult`, so the checkbox mapping cannot drift.
- **E2E (Playwright web + Electron)**: hotkey → modal → Tab, Enter → engaged → order attempt refused → unfreeze with step-up. Shared suite in E39-Q02.
- **a11y**: axe-core on the modal and `/admin/risk-policy`; manual screen-reader pass verifying `alertdialog` semantics, the restated consequence, focus starting on cancel, and the keyboard hold equivalent.
- **Security**: E39-X02 abuse cases; this story includes a test that a client-forced enable of a disabled control still yields 403.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
These controls are the UI for the product's last-resort safety mechanism, so the threats are: an accidental freeze (mitigated by the blast-radius confirm with focus on Cancel, safe defaults, and the hotkey opening rather than firing); a *malicious* freeze to strand a trader (mitigated server-side by RBAC scope and audit, surfaced here by always naming the actor and reason); and an unauthorised **release** (mitigated by owner-only + step-up, enforced server-side — the UI's role is to make the step-up explicit, never to be the gate). SCR-134 saves are step-up gated per SR-025 ("changing risk caps or per-account profiles"). No secrets are rendered. `security` label mandatory per DoD §8.

## Accessibility notes
`role="alertdialog"` on SCR-072 with the consequence restated in text; focus starts on the **cancel** control; single blast-radius confirm (CMP-044 `variant="standard"`, CMP-211 `confirmMode: "single"` for the kill switch); hold-to-confirm exposes `aria-valuenow` progress and has a keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`); panic buttons are never icon-only and carry scope in their accessible name; SCR-134 uses fieldsets per limit with units and the current measured value beside the limit, a radio group for enforcement scope, and each limit has a description of what happens on breach. Danger/confirm patterns must be announced — an explicit R3 a11y gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).

## Performance notes
The modal must render and be interactive within 100 ms of the hotkey press. The freeze is one backend call halting acceptance server-side within 200 ms; the UI must not appear blocked while per-account results stream in (SCR-072 performance note). SCR-134 confirms only after server acknowledgement, with policy changes effective on the next evaluation cycle (≤2 s).

## Observability
Audit via CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger on every invocation: `risk.freeze` (with the full option set), `risk.unfreeze`, `risk_policy.updated`, `panic.flatten_all`. Client metrics: modal open→confirm duration (to detect a confirmation flow that is too slow in an emergency), and hotkey usage counts.

title: Implement the M17 risk evaluator core with rolling per-account counters
body:
## Context
Module **M17** is the risk/limit enforcement layer named in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 for E39 and in `20-architecture.md` §3.10 as part of the OMS `Validator` responsibilities ("per-account and per-manager risk caps, kill-switch state"). This Task builds its **core**: a pure decision function plus the stateful service that feeds it. Wiring it into the order path is E39-S01; lockouts are E39-S02; the kill-switch is E39-S03. Splitting it this way keeps every ticket ≤8 points and lets the pure evaluator be exhaustively unit-tested before any I/O exists.

Architecture principle P8 (`20-architecture.md` §1) is the reason this is backend-only: "The frontend is never trusted for account scope, risk caps or environment."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Package `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/` containing:
  - `evaluator.py` — **pure** `evaluate(state: AccountRiskState, caps: ResolvedCaps, cmd: OrderCommand) -> RiskDecision`. No I/O, no clock reads (time is passed in), fully deterministic.
  - `caps.py` — cap resolution: merge the global `risk_policy` row, the account's `account_profiles` caps, and the per-manager override `user_account_access.max_daily_loss_usd`, taking the **most restrictive** value per cap. Resolution order and tie-breaking documented in-module and in `24-internal-schemas.md`.
  - `state.py` — `RiskService` maintaining per-account rolling counters: realised PnL today, unrealised PnL, open position count, gross notional per symbol and in aggregate, orders submitted in the trailing 60 s, consecutive losing closes. Fed from the `oms.*` event bus (order/execution/position events) with a periodic reconcile from `position_snapshots` (`reason='risk_eval'`).
  - `clock.py` — day-boundary arithmetic honouring `risk_policy.day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes`, per the E39-K01 decision.
- Caps evaluated: `max_position_notional_usd`, `max_open_positions`, `max_daily_loss_usd` / `max_daily_loss_pct`, `max_drawdown_pct`, `max_orders_per_minute`, `max_consecutive_losses`, `max_leverage`, per-symbol concentration, and `allowed_symbols`/`blocked_symbols` (from `account_profiles`).
- `RiskDecision` carries `allowed: bool`, `code` (`risk_limit_breached` | `account_locked` | `trading_disabled` | `risk_state_unavailable` | `symbol_not_allowed`), a human-readable `message` naming cap, limit and current value ("would exceed max position 0.5 BTC (current 0.4)" — the exact shape US-PROF-004 requires), and a machine-readable `cap`, `limit`, `actual` triple for the UI.
- **Reduce-only exemption**: reduce-only and position-closing commands are *always* permitted by cap checks (US-PROF-004: "reduce-only orders are still allowed"; US-ADMIN-003: "reduce-only actions remain available"). This is a first-class branch in the evaluator with its own tests.
- **Fail-closed**: if `RiskService` cannot produce a fresh state for an account (staleness beyond a configured `risk_state_max_age_seconds`, default 10 s), `evaluate` returns `allowed=False, code=risk_state_unavailable`.
- Metrics and structured logging as listed under Observability.

## Out of scope
- The `Validator` integration and API error mapping (E39-S01).
- Creating/releasing lockout rows and their side effects (E39-S02).
- Kill-switch state reads (E39-S03 provides the port; `evaluate` receives its result as an input).
- Any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Position notional cap
  Given resolved caps with max_position_notional_usd 25000 and state holding 20000
  When evaluate is called with a command adding 10000 of notional
  Then the decision is not allowed with code risk_limit_breached
  And the message names the cap, the limit 25000 and the current value 20000

Scenario: Reduce-only is never capped
  Given an account in lockout and at every cap simultaneously
  When evaluate is called with a reduce-only close command
  Then the decision is allowed

Scenario: Most restrictive cap wins
  Given a global policy cap of 1000, a profile cap of 800 and a per-manager override of 500
  When caps are resolved
  Then the effective max_daily_loss_usd is 500
  And the decision message attributes the breach to the manager override

Scenario (failure): Stale state fails closed
  Given the account's risk state is older than risk_state_max_age_seconds
  When evaluate is called with any opening command
  Then the decision is not allowed with code risk_state_unavailable

Scenario (edge): Day boundary rollover
  Given realised loss of -1400 recorded before the configured day boundary
  When the boundary passes
  Then the daily counter resets to 0 and a previously blocking daily-loss cap no longer blocks
```

## Technical notes / design
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RiskDecision:
    allowed: bool
    code: str | None
    message: str | None
    cap: str | None
    limit: Decimal | None
    actual: Decimal | None
    evaluated_at: datetime
```
The evaluator runs checks in a fixed order (symbol allow/block → kill-switch → lockout → orders-per-minute → open positions → position notional → concentration → leverage → daily loss → drawdown → consecutive losses) and returns on the **first** failure, so the message is deterministic and testable; the order is documented and asserted by a test so it cannot drift.

`RiskService` keeps counters in memory with a Postgres-backed rebuild on startup (replaying today's `executions` and current `positions`), so a restart mid-day cannot silently reset a daily-loss counter — a restart that cannot rebuild leaves accounts in `risk_state_unavailable` (fail-closed) rather than in a permissive zero state. This is a deliberate, tested behaviour.

Config keys (`cvapi.settings`): `risk.state_max_age_seconds` (default 10), `risk.eval_interval_seconds` (default 5, satisfying US-RULE-012's "at least every 5 s"), `risk.counter_rebuild_on_startup` (default true).

## Test plan
- **Unit (exhaustive decision table)**: one test per cap × {under, at, over} × {opening, reduce-only} — the evaluator is pure, so this is cheap and is the primary safety net. Includes cap-resolution precedence, check-order assertion, and message formatting.
- **Unit (clock)**: day-boundary arithmetic across DST-free UTC offsets, boundary exactly at an event timestamp, and a rollover mid-evaluation.
- **Unit (state)**: counter updates from a synthetic `oms.*` event sequence including partial fills, a reversal, and a late fee settlement; startup rebuild from a seeded DB; staleness detection.
- **Integration**: against recorded Bybit demo fixtures (partial fills and a rejection) asserting counters track `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` within the tolerance chosen by E39-K01.
- **Perf micro-benchmark**: `evaluate` p95 ≤1 ms in isolation (leaving headroom inside the ≤5 ms end-to-end budget), asserted in CI with a regression gate.
- Coverage target: **≥90 %** on `cvapi/oms/risk/` per the R3 local policy for security-relevant modules.

## Security notes
Threats from `04-security-program.md`: tampering (a client-supplied value influencing a cap) — the evaluator accepts caps only from the database, never from the request body; elevation of privilege (a manager's override loosening a cap) — resolution takes the most restrictive value, and a test asserts an override can never *widen* a cap, matching US-PROF-003's "overrides never widen a hard risk cap"; denial of service (an unbounded counter rebuild) — the rebuild is bounded to today's window with a query timeout. Data classification: financial state, no secrets. `security` label required; Security engineer review is a merge gate.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Budget: the full order-path risk check adds ≤5 ms p95 (US-PROF-004 / US-ADMIN-003 NFRs), inside budget #4 (order submit → ack p95 <300 ms on demo, a hard R3 gate per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2). title: Postgres migrations and internal schemas for risk_lockouts, risk_policy and kill_switch_state
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` already carries the *inputs* to risk enforcement — the cap columns on `account_profiles` (§3.3: `max_position_notional_usd`, `max_daily_loss_usd`, `max_open_positions`, `max_orders_per_minute`) and the per-manager freeze columns on `user_account_access` (§3.1.3: `frozen`, `frozen_at`, `frozen_by`, `frozen_reason`, `max_daily_loss_usd`). It does **not** yet carry the *state* E39 produces: active lockouts with their reason and expiry, the global risk policy configured on SCR-134, and the kill-switch's own persisted state.

This is an interface-first Task per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10: the schema diff is drafted and reviewed before E39-T01 implements against it, because three other epics (E30 ticket headroom, E34 fan-out pre-validation, E42 admin screens) read these shapes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration adding:
  - **`risk_lockouts`** — `id uuid PK`, `exchange_account_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES exchange_accounts(id)`, `user_id uuid NULL REFERENCES users(id)` (for per-manager lockouts), `reason text NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('daily_loss','consecutive_losses','max_positions','manual'))` — matching the `RiskSummary.accounts[].lockout.reason` enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `threshold numeric(38,18)`, `actual_value numeric(38,18)`, `since timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `until timestamptz NULL` (NULL = until day boundary), `released_at timestamptz NULL`, `released_by uuid NULL REFERENCES users(id)`, `release_reason text NULL`, `actions_taken jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` (orders cancelled / positions flattened counts). Partial unique index guaranteeing at most one active lockout per (account, user) pair: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_risk_lockout_active ON risk_lockouts (exchange_account_id, coalesce(user_id,'00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid)) WHERE released_at IS NULL;`
  - **`risk_policy`** — the single global policy row set from SCR-134: `id uuid PK`, `singleton boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true UNIQUE CHECK (singleton)`, `max_total_notional_usd`, `max_daily_loss_usd`, `max_drawdown_pct`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage`, `max_orders_per_minute`, `per_symbol_concentration_pct`, `breach_behaviour jsonb NOT NULL` (per-limit `warn|block|flatten`), `lockout_minutes_default smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 60` (bounded 0..1440, matching `RiskCaps.lockout_minutes_after_breach`), `block_trading_when_degraded boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, `day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `updated_by`, `updated_at`.
  - **`kill_switch_state`** — `scope text NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('global','accounts'))`, `exchange_account_id uuid NULL`, `engaged boolean NOT NULL`, `engaged_at`, `engaged_by`, `reason text`, `options jsonb` (the `SetKillSwitchRequest` option set), with a unique index on `(scope, coalesce(exchange_account_id, ...))` so global engagement is a single row.
- `CHECK` constraints mirroring the OpenAPI bounds exactly (`max_orders_per_minute` 1..600, `lockout_minutes_after_breach` 0..1440, `max_open_positions` 0..100) so the database refuses values the API would accept through a bug.
- Pydantic/dataclass models in `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/models.py` and a documented section added to `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` describing `RiskDecision`, `LockoutState` and `KillSwitchState` as domain objects.
- Down-migration, and a seed of the `risk_policy` singleton with conservative defaults (every limit set, `block_trading_when_degraded=true`).
- Update `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` with the new tables, the ERD edge additions, and their retention statement (risk state is retained indefinitely — it is part of the accountability trail alongside `audit_log`).

## Out of scope
- The evaluator logic (E39-T01) and any endpoint (E39-S01..S03).
- QuestDB/Parquet changes — risk state is relational only.
- Migrating existing data: R3 is pre-production; there is no legacy risk state.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given a database at the previous head
  When the migration is applied and then downgraded
  Then both complete without error and the schema matches the before/after snapshots

Scenario: At most one active lockout per account
  Given an active lockout exists for account A with user_id NULL
  When a second unreleased lockout row for the same pair is inserted
  Then the insert is refused by the unique index

Scenario: Bounds are enforced at the database level
  Given an attempt to write max_orders_per_minute = 900
  Then the CHECK constraint rejects it, independent of API validation

Scenario (edge): Singleton risk policy
  Given the risk_policy row exists
  When a second row is inserted
  Then the unique singleton constraint refuses it
```

## Technical notes / design
Migration id `e39_risk_state`, placed after the E28 profile migration in the Alembic chain. Timestamps are `timestamptz`; money is `numeric(38,18)` to match the rest of the schema; percentages are `numeric(9,6)`. `actions_taken` and `breach_behaviour` are `jsonb` because their shape is owned by the API contract and must not require a migration per added action counter — but each key is documented in `24-internal-schemas.md`.

`day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes` exists because US-POS-009 requires "today" to use "the configured day boundary consistently with the daily-loss limit"; its default of 0 (UTC) matches `24-internal-schemas.md` §11 `sys.daily_loss_lockout`. E39-K01's decision may constrain the allowed range; if so, tighten the CHECK in this migration.

## Test plan
- Unit: model round-trip (`RiskDecision`, `LockoutState`, `KillSwitchState`) serialise/deserialise; bound validation mirrors the CHECKs.
- Migration test: apply on an empty DB and on a seeded DB, then downgrade, asserting schema equality with the snapshot (existing `tests/migrations/` harness).
- Constraint tests: one test per CHECK and per unique index asserting the exact `SQLSTATE`.
- Coverage: ≥90 % on `cvapi/oms/risk/models.py` (M17 local policy).

## Security notes
`risk_lockouts.release_reason` is user-supplied free text rendered in the audit log and SCR-071 — it must be stored raw and escaped at render, never interpolated into SQL (parameterised queries only) or into log format strings. No secrets in any new column. `kill_switch_state` is security-critical state: the migration grants no UPDATE/DELETE to any non-owner application role beyond the risk service's own role, consistent with the least-privilege model in `04-security-program.md`. `security` label applies (the Task adds tables on the OMS safety path).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Indexes: `ix_risk_lockouts_account_active` (partial, `WHERE released_at IS NULL`) so the hot-path lockout lookup is an index-only probe well inside the ≤5 ms evaluator budget; `kill_switch_state` is a ≤N-row table read through the 5 s cache, so it needs no special indexing beyond its unique key.

## Observability
Migration emits a `system_events` row on apply. The seeded policy write emits `risk_policy.updated` with actor `system` so the audit chain starts consistent.

- [ ] Migration applies/reverses in CI; snapshot test green.
- [ ] Constraint tests cover every CHECK and unique index.

title: ADR-0016 risk enforcement model plus the flatten-all runbook and doc updates
body:
## Context
Two documentation obligations fall out of E39 and are explicitly required rather than optional.

First, the roadmap's E39 row (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2) specifies the kill-switch semantics "stops new risk, does not force-close" **"plus a separate documented flatten-all runbook"**. That runbook does not exist yet and is a deliverable of this epic, not of E29.

Second, `docs/plan/27-adrs/` has no ADR covering risk enforcement. The decisions made in E39-K01 (authoritative daily-PnL source, day boundary) and E39-T01 (cap-resolution precedence, check ordering, fail-closed posture) are exactly the kind of non-obvious, cross-epic decisions the ADR index exists to record — E30, E34, E35, E42 and E44 all build on them. The DoR/DoD for Spikes (§5.2) also requires the spike's decision to be recorded as an ADR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0027-risk-enforcement-and-kill-switch.md`**, status `decided`, following the existing ADR template, covering: server-side-only enforcement (P8) and why client-side pre-checks are advisory only; the authoritative daily-PnL source and day-boundary semantics from E39-K01; cap-resolution precedence (most restrictive wins; overrides never widen); the fixed check order and why message determinism matters; fail-closed on stale risk state and on unreadable kill-switch state; the "stops new risk, does not force-close" kill-switch semantics and why flatten is opt-in; step-up gating per SR-025. Consequences section names the downstream epics that rely on each decision.
- Add ADR-0016 to the ADR index table in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §13.
- **`docs/runbooks/flatten-all.md`** — the operational runbook: when to use flatten-all instead of (or after) the kill-switch; the exact sequence (engage kill-switch → verify no new orders are being accepted → `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all` with `cancel_open_orders: true` → verify via `GET /api/v1/positions` and `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` that `open_positions` is 0 and `positions_without_native_stop` is 0 → record the incident); what to do when some accounts fail (per-account retry, and the escalation path if an account remains stale); the demo-vs-live differences (demo is REST-only for order entry, so flatten is REST-driven in both but latency differs); and the post-incident audit query showing every `risk.freeze`, `panic.flatten_all` and `position.flattened` row for the window.
- Drill instruction: the runbook is exercised as part of E39-Q03's chaos scenarios and again during the R3 soak; the runbook states its own rehearsal cadence.
- Update `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10 (`Validator`, `KillSwitch` rows) and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11/§12 so they describe what shipped, not what was proposed.
- Update `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` if E39-S01..S03 introduced any deviation (notably the `risk_state_unavailable` problem type).

## Out of scope
- User-facing help content for SCR-071/073 (ships with E39-S04's copy).
- The security program document itself (E39-X02 updates it if the threat model changes controls).
- Release notes / changelog fragments (handled per story).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: ADR captures every cross-epic decision
  Given ADR-0016 is submitted
  Then it records the daily-PnL source, the day boundary, cap precedence, check order, fail-closed posture and kill-switch semantics
  And each decision names the downstream epics that depend on it

Scenario: Runbook is executable by someone who did not build the system
  Given an engineer unfamiliar with E39 follows docs/runbooks/flatten-all.md on the demo environment
  When they reach the end
  Then all positions are flat, all working orders are cancelled, and they have produced the audit query output
  And they needed no clarification from the E39 authors

Scenario (failure): Partial flatten
  Given one account's REST path fails during the runbook
  Then the runbook states the retry procedure and the escalation threshold explicitly
  And it states that the kill-switch remains engaged until reconciliation confirms the account's true state

Scenario: Docs match shipped behaviour
  Given E39-S01..S03 are merged
  Then 20-architecture.md, 24-internal-schemas.md, 22-api-openapi.yaml and 23-ws-protocol.md describe the shipped behaviour
  And the traceability CI check passes
```

## Technical notes / design
The runbook is written as a numbered checklist with copy-pasteable `curl` calls against `/api/v1`, each showing the expected response shape, plus the verification query:
```sql
SELECT ts, actor, action, target, severity
FROM audit_log
WHERE action IN ('risk.freeze','risk.unfreeze','panic.flatten_all','position.flattened','risk.lockout_triggered')
  AND ts BETWEEN :from AND :to
ORDER BY id;
```

  2. Manager or viewer releases an engaged kill-switch → must 403 regardless of scope.
  3. Owner releases the kill-switch without a valid step-up token → must 403 (SR-025).
  4. Manager clears their own lockout → must 403; the owner is notified; the attempt is audited.
  5. Replay a captured override request with its original idempotency key → must return the stored result and must not re-release a *new* lockout.
  6. Submit an order carrying `risk_caps` / `max_daily_loss_usd` in the body → the values are ignored, and the attempt is logged.

  10. Direct UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_log` rows describing a freeze → refused by the grant model, and the attempt itself recorded (US-ADMIN-008).
  11. Tighten a cap and immediately attempt to force-close another user's position through the tightened path → confirms the "no forced liquidation" semantics are not abusable.
  12. Induce `risk_state_unavailable` under load and confirm the system refuses rather than admits (availability-abuse case, results reused from E39-Q03).
- **SAST/DAST rules**: Semgrep rules asserting (a) no order-submission code path exists that does not call the risk gate (pattern over `OrderCommand` construction sites), (b) no code reads caps from a request body, (c) no `kill_switch` read bypasses the fail-closed helper. Scenario: Enforcement cannot be disabled
```gherkin
  Given an owner with full admin rights attempts to disable risk enforcement via feature flags

Scenario: No account enumeration

  Given any abuse case produces an unintended state change

  And the R3 security gate cannot pass until it is closed

Scenario: Static rules have teeth

```

Abuse cases 1–7 and 9–11 are added to `tests/security/e39/` and run in the standard CI security job; case 8 (forged WS frame) is executed with a local proxy injecting frames, and case 12 reuses the E39-Q03 load harness. title: Foreign-fill freeze setter: reconciliation_foreign_order lockout (SR-E27-19)
body:
## Context

This is a plan gap, filed by the orchestrator's ruling (LANE-28, 2026-10-22 22:15Z, Q2). Threat SR-E27-19 requires that a fill or order the OMS did not place (a foreign one) freezes trading on that account until an owner acknowledges it.

`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §8 names the lockout reason `reconciliation_foreign_order`, but no ticket, no `21` row and no code owns its setter. E29-T05 (#848) detects the foreign fill. Until this ticket lands, T05 binds a paging lockout (P1 plus audit, no freeze), and SR-E27-19 stays open in the threat model.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **The lockout reason `reconciliation_foreign_order`** in E39's lockout, as `ForeignOrderLockout.open(account_id, *, finding, key)` (T04's port, #4152) bound to a real freeze.
- **Effect:** no new order on the account until an owner acknowledges; cancels and reduce-only exits stay allowed.
- **Audit:** the setter and the acknowledgement each write an append-only audit record (C-2.9).
- **The schema:** a `21` schema row or column, if the lockout state needs one, through a migration under C-5.x.

## Out of scope

- detecting the foreign fill (E29-T05);
- the UI notice (E39-S04);
- the kill switch (E39-S03).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: A foreign fill freezes the account
  Given an account with no open order of the OMS's own
  When the private stream delivers a fill the OMS did not place
  Then the account is locked out with reason reconciliation_foreign_order
  And no new order is accepted on it until an owner acknowledges
  And the lockout and the acknowledgement are each audited

Scenario: Exits stay possible while frozen
  Given an account frozen for a foreign fill
  When a reduce-only exit or a cancel is submitted
  Then it is accepted, and the native stop-loss invariant still holds (C-2.6)

Scenario: Failure case - the setter cannot persist
  Given the lockout store is unavailable
  When a foreign fill is detected
  Then the order path for that account fails closed and an owner is paged
```

## Technical notes / design

The setter is the risk module's one writer of the freeze (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.10): `ForeignOrderLockout.open(account_id, *, finding, key)`, the port E29-T04 declares in `oms/ports.py` (#4152) and E29-T05 and E29-T06 call. It is idempotent where the lockout is open already, and opens once per finding, keyed by the order's `orderId` or the fill's `exec_id`, so the Owner's release sticks. The freeze is a `risk_lockouts` row with the reason `reconciliation_foreign_order`, account scope (`user_id` null) and no `until`, so no clock releases it; only the Owner releases it, through E39's release path (`overrideRiskLockout`), never automatically. New orders are refused with the same 403 problem as any risk lockout (`account_locked`, E39-S01); cancels and reduce-only exits pass, and the native stop-loss invariant holds on them (C-2.6). It is a synchronous check ahead of any interpreter (C-2.21), and it is not B19's `stale_lockout`: each refuses on its own, and clearing one leaves the other.
E29-T06's contract-first PR, with E39, adds the reason to `LockoutReason` (§8.11), `rl_reason` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.11), `RiskSummary`'s lockout reason (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) and the B20 chart (`28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B20, its machine JSON and `machine_hashes.lock`) before this code (C-6.1). It also makes the freeze hold beside any other lockout of the account, because `ux_risk_lockout_active` admits one active row per account and manager: as the table stands, an account already locked for daily loss could not take the freeze, which would be lost when that lockout ends. This ticket binds the setter to that contract; a column or an index the lockout state needs goes through one migration (C-5.x).
Until this ticket lands, E29-T05 binds a paging stand-in (a P1 page and an audit record, no freeze) and SR-E27-19 stays open in the threat model; this binding replaces it.

## Test plan

- Unit: the setter is idempotent where the lockout is open, and opens once per finding key, so the same `orderId` or `exec_id` seen again after the Owner's release does not reopen it.
- Unit: with the freeze open, a new order is refused with `account_locked`; a cancel and a reduce-only exit pass, with an explicit assertion that the native stop-loss invariant holds on that path (C-2.6).
- Failure case: with the lockout store unavailable, the account's order path fails closed and an owner is paged.

title: Host-console kill-switch fallback `candleviewer kill` (SR-086)
body:
## Context

This is a plan gap, filed by the orchestrator's ruling on #5032 (2026-10-30 05:27Z) under the filing-freeze exception for a security and plan gap. The Fable security lens found it (SEC-10B-01) while reviewing SCR-157's blocking dialog (E10-S04, #306): no ticket builds the host-console fallback that the dialog names as its exit.

SR-086 (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` :1051) makes it a MUST: a documented CLI command, executable on the trading host without the web UI, that performs the same actions when the UI or the tailnet is unavailable. §9.3 (:1404) gives it as `candleviewer kill --scope all --mode cancel`, using the same service code path, and N5 (:480) and RR-03 (:1914) rely on it for a Tailscale or ISP outage with a position open. The E39 threat model records the hole (G-8) and the control (SR-E39-16: a local channel only the service user can open, engage-only). The surfaces already print the command: SCR-157 and SCR-159 (E10-D03 §9.1 :309, §9.2 :318; `apps/web/src/features/system-states/copy.ts`:140), E39-D01 §7.5 (:454) as the exit when REST is unreachable, E17-D01 §6 (:193) with E10-D03 :309 as the only exit while the protocol is incompatible, and E39-D03's copy deck S5 (:196) in the offline cluster's reason. The command does not exist.

#306 (E10-S04) and E39-S05 consume it: #5032 requires the dialog's exit to be ticketed before the dialog can show on a live account, and #306's QA record names this ticket a precondition.

**Placement (orchestrator, 2026-10-30):** a precondition for live enablement; demo does not need it. So it is planned in R4, in Sprint 20, the first sprint in R4's window with room for its three points, and E39-S03 stays its blocker.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **The command `candleviewer kill`**, run on the trading host with no web UI and no tailnet: `candleviewer kill --scope all --mode cancel` (04 :1404); the bare form that SCR-157 and SCR-159 print does the same. No `candleviewer` command exists yet: `services/api/pyproject.toml` has no `[project.scripts]`, and the host CLIs run as `python -m candleviewer.<module>`, for example `candleviewer.breakglass` (E09-S11).
- **The channel (SR-E39-16):** a local channel only the service user can open, with peer credentials checked. The command is a thin client of the running API, which engages in-process first and persists after (SR-E39-05). It holds no key and signs nothing.
- **The same code path and audit record:** the console calls E39-S03's `KillSwitchService` engage (the service behind `POST /trading/kill-switch`), never a second implementation, so it writes the records the REST engage writes, one per affected entity (US-RULE-014). The actor is the console: `actor_type=system`, the OS user and the host (SR-E39-16, RK-S05).
- **Idempotent (SR-083):** a second run is harmless.
- **Engage-only:** no release, unfreeze or override verb; release stays on the API with step-up, in the UI (SR-084, SR-E39-08).
- **API down:** the command says so and exits non-zero. It calls no exchange endpoint (SR-E39-16).
- **Documentation:** the console's section of the flatten-all runbook (E39-T03): the command, its arguments, what it does not do, and where a release is done.

## Out of scope

- the kill-switch engine, the REST engage and its state (E39-S03), which this ticket calls;
- release, unfreeze and override from the console (SR-084, SR-E39-16);
- other scopes and modes: 04 :1404 documents `--scope all --mode cancel` only, and the console has no identity to authorise a flatten (SR-081 (4), RK-S05);
- the in-app controls (E39-S05) and the SCR-157 and SCR-159 blocks that print the command (E10-S04, #306, built);
- the rest of the runbook and its exchange-side fallback for a down API (E39-T03).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: It engages from the trading host without the web UI or the tailnet
  Given the web UI and the tailnet are unavailable
  When the operator runs `candleviewer kill --scope all --mode cancel` on the trading host
  Then the kill switch is engaged globally and new orders are refused
  And working orders are cancelled and no position is closed

Scenario: It takes the REST engage's code path and writes its audit record
  Given a kill switch engaged once over REST and once from the console
  When the two engagements are compared
  Then both called the same KillSwitchService engage with the same options
  And both wrote the same records, one per affected entity
  And the console's records name the console as the actor: system, the OS user and the host

Scenario: Idempotent - running it again is harmless
  Given the kill switch is already engaged globally
  When the operator runs the same command again
  Then the switch stays engaged and the run reports that the engagement is already in force
  And nothing the first run cancelled is cancelled again

Scenario: Engage-only - a release is refused from the console
  Given the kill switch is engaged
  When a release is attempted through the console or its channel
  Then it is refused and the switch stays engaged
  And a release stays an Owner action on the API, with step-up, in the UI

Scenario: The fallback is documented
  Given the flatten-all runbook (E39-T03)
  When an operator reads it with the API unreachable
  Then it names `candleviewer kill`, its arguments and that it only engages
  And it says where a release is done
  And its command line is the one SCR-157 and SCR-159 print
```

## Technical notes / design

The console is a thin client in the pattern of `services/api/candleviewer/breakglass.py` (a host CLI that imports neither `secrets`, C-3.2, nor `audit`, C-3.3) with the opposite lifecycle: break-glass runs while cv-api is stopped, and this command reaches the running API. The `candleviewer` command, its `kill` subcommand and a `[project.scripts]` entry in `services/api/pyproject.toml` are new. The pages print the bare `candleviewer kill`, so the bare form must do what 04 :1404's explicit form does: `--scope all` is the REST engage's `global` scope and `--mode cancel` its default options (`cancel_open_orders` true, `flatten_positions` false, `disarm_rules` true; `SetKillSwitchRequest` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`).

The channel is the model's TB-K5 (§2): a local channel only the service user can open, peer credentials checked (SR-E39-16). A Unix-domain socket gives peer credentials and a TCP port does not, so the PR records its choice and why. The API engages in-process first and persists after (SR-E39-05), a synchronous check ahead of any interpreter (C-2.21), and the reply says whether it persisted (`persisted` on `KillSwitchResult` is E39-S03's gap G-12). Postgres, the audit lane, the idempotency store, the WS broadcast and the exchange never refuse or delay it (SR-E39-05). `SetKillSwitchRequest` requires a `reason` and an idempotency key: the console supplies a key per run and a default reason that names the console, so neither can fail an engage.

The console enters at SR-E39-08's one authorisation function. It can only engage, so that function's role × scope × direction × path matrix (`test_kill_switch_role_scope_direction_path_matrix`) gains the host-console path, where release and override are refused in code. The audit entry path is the console's value in the vocabulary SR-E39-12 registers with E39-S03; if S03 registered none, ask on S03's issue and never invent one. The console only calls the service, which drives B18, so the chart and `machine_hashes.lock` stay as they are.

## Test plan

- Unit: `test_console_release_is_refused` and `test_console_channel_refuses_another_uid` (SR-E39-16), and the host-console rows of `test_kill_switch_role_scope_direction_path_matrix` (SR-E39-08).
- Unit: the console and the REST handler reach the same `KillSwitchService` engage, and their records match except the actor and the entry path.
- Unit: a second run reports the engagement in force and cancels nothing the first run cancelled, on recorded fixtures (C-13.5), with no network.
- Failure case: with the API down, the command says so, exits non-zero and calls no exchange endpoint.
- The console engage cancels no protective order: an explicit assertion that the native stop-loss stays (C-2.6; SR-E39-06).
- Integration (`@pytest.mark.integration`): against the real Postgres the console engage persists the state row, and it holds with Postgres down (SR-E39-05).
- Docs: the runbook prints the command exactly as SCR-157 and SCR-159 do.
- Drill (SR-086's verification; SR-087): on the demo stack with the web UI and the tailnet down, with the timings against 04 §9.3's targets recorded in the PRR (`07-release-and-prr.md`).
- Coverage ≥95% line plus `mutmut` on the console's channel and authorisation code (C-13.1).

## Security notes

- This is C-10.2: the risk module, where the kill switch lives. It needs a `security-review` reviewer.
- It is the path of TB-K5 (§2): RK-S05 (the console acts with no identity, and "the same actions" would let it release), RK-S06 (a host process abuses its channel) and RK-E02 (one authorisation function on every entry path). SR-E39-16 is the control and AC-RK-19 its abuse case (E39-X02).
- Engage-only by construction: no identity, no key, no `secrets` import, nothing signed. The worst use of it is a stop, never a start. A refused release or another user's connection is a security event (SR-E39-08).
- It enforces synchronously before any interpreter (C-2.21). No flag, setting, rule or environment variable turns it off or widens it (SR-E39-07, C-4.14).
- The record and the log hold the OS user, the host, the scope and the options, never a credential (C-2.9, C-12.6).

## Accessibility notes

N/A — a command-line tool. Its output is plain text lines with no colour-only signal. The SCR-157 and SCR-159 blocks that print the command are E10-S04's (#306).

## Performance notes

The console adds one local hop, so E39-S03's budgets hold: the server-side halt within 200 ms of the call, and the whole kill within 5 s under normal exchange conditions (SR-080). The drill measures 04 §9.3's targets through the console: block ≤1 s, cancel-all issued to all accounts ≤5 s, confirmed clean ≤30 s.

## Observability

A console engage is counted in E39-S03's kill-switch series (`cv_kill_switch_engaged`, `cv_kill_switch_transitions_total`) and pages like any engage (`cv_kill_switch_engaged == 1`), the route to SR-085's out-of-band Owner alert. The log line carries the OS user, the host, the scope, the options and the outcome, never a credential (C-12.6); a refused release or another user's connection logs a security event (SR-E39-08). No new metric series is required.
